title: Five column-count buckets published on <html> (data-bucket, --cols, view.bucket)
description: Operator 2026-10-05 (ph-mdqo, DESIGN §10.12): the layout solves a problem over widths, never per width. Five buckets derived from one unit, the layout column = 2 rem (the grid cell at 1x DPR and the default scale, 36 px at 100 %; follows UI scale and browser text size, never DPR). cols = floor(innerWidth / 2rem). A field floor is 8 columns; the bucket counts field floors across the window, doubling: 1 watch (cols < 8), 2 phone (8-15), 3 tablet (16-31), 4 desk (32-63), 5 wide (64+). The renderer class (rclass.js, RFC-062 draft) still picks the nav model; the bucket decides projection inside it. Other lanes read ONLY :root[data-bucket="N"] in CSS and view.bucket in JS; nobody else reads window width for layout.

description: Operator 2026-10-05: a big pass with rules. 1428x900 (launch size) · page frame · .app pads left/right by --gap (12 px) and .frame pulls itself out by -5 px to meet the hero panel's outline, so the bottom status row floats 12 px in from the window corners and the content column stops short of the right edge. Operator measured: .app 0 and .frame 0 fix it, footer meets the corners. Cause: the hero panel's og-panel outline (4 px offset + 1 px) was the thing the page aligned to; with the margin gone the content's inner right edge now needs the same 2 px edge treatment the left has (to confirm which: the rail's 2 px gap/grid). Rule candidate: one frame padding token on all four sides, chrome (strip, footer) full-bleed, the hero's outline inside the frame rather than the frame outside the outline (ph-p43h).
all widths · sidebar scroll recess (.rail [data-shade]) · (a) the shade stops short of the rail's corners: the rail has 6 px padding and a radius, the sticky ::before/::after sit inside the padding box so the gradient ends 6 px in and the rounded corner shows a gap; (b) the ink is rgba(0,0,0,.95) over --bg-raised, reads heavy: operator wants a tint (shade ink from the theme, e.g. --bg-sunken or the accent at low alpha, not pure black); (c) bottom edge flickers in the last few px when not scrolled to the end: the ::after carries margin-top -24 px inside a flex column with a 2 px gap, and scrollshade toggles data-shade-bottom at scrollHeight - 1 px, so sub-pixel scroll positions flip the attribute and the last row shifts by the gap. The trick itself works (operator: noticed it without noticing it). Rule candidate: shades drawn by the scroller's own overlay element that covers padding and radius (inset 0 of the scroller, clip-path to the radius), ink = theme token, hysteresis of 2 px on the toggle (ph-p43h / ph-acnj).
1428x900 · hero rail (HeroStrip: numeral + planned target/lag/speed + plan strip with position bar and ruler) · takes roughly a third of the window height at the launch size and a larger share as the window shrinks; it is a fixed-height stack with no budget relative to the viewport. Over widths: the share grows as height shrinks because the rail never gives anything up. Rule candidate for 10.12: the hero has a height budget per bucket (a fraction of the viewport with a floor), the numeral scales within the budget (HeroNumerals already derives font-size from --num-h), and the plan strip's two rows (bar, ruler) become one row under the budget; the strip's e-stop/pause pair never moves (RENDERING row 11).
1428x900 · category pages (Motion: Limits / Settings on trial / Ceiling overrides) · every card lays itself out by a different rule: LimitsWidget is a role composite with its own repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px,1fr)) grid and two bright sub-group titles inside the card (88 px row pitch, columns fill the width); the trial list is a chip list; the Ceiling overrides card is plain fields placed in cell-quantized columns, so the last ~116 px of card width is an empty gutter and its rows are 55 px; the page's '3 advanced / Reset' row sits outside any card 4 px left of the card edge; column gaps 15 vs 12 px. Same pattern in AdvancedGeneratorWidget and PatternWidget (each a private auto-fit grid). Rule candidate: ONE card-body layout for fields and composites alike: columns come from the bucket (cell-quantized), the row's remainder stretches so no card ends in a gutter, one row height per presentation (ph-z50z rungs), sub-group titles and section headers are one type step each and nowhere else, composites may not carry a private grid rule (ph-acnj lint catches grid-template-columns in src/ui/hero and plugins). Page-level actions (advanced toggle, Reset) move with ph-lxea's head controls.
1428x900 · frame edges (operator's '2 px grid thing on the right'): devtools shows the rail/content gap as the .frame grid gap (12 px) with 2 / -2 markers from the rail's recess shades (margin cancels the rail's 2 px flex gap); the content's right edge ends ~8 px short of the frame with no treatment and the status row starts 14 px in from the left and ~45 px short on the right (its own padding + the scale control). Sidebar box margins are 11 px left vs 16 px right. Pending the operator's confirmation of which left-edge treatment the right edge should mirror. Folds into ph-p43h: one frame token, edges symmetric, status row full-bleed with the same token.
Frame edge (screenshot 37, devtools on div.frame 1428x530): the frame grid puts its --gap (12 px) between the rail and the content column and padding-top above both, but the content column has no right inset at all: its right edge sits on the window edge (margin-right is even -5px for the hero outline). Ruling: the content column gets the same 12 px gap on the right that it has on the left (symmetric inset), so the page frame is rail | gap | content | gap. Goes with the earlier app/frame 0-margin item (ph-p43h): once the app's 12 px side margins go to 0, this right gap is what keeps the content off the edge. The 'two-pixel grid' phrase meant the devtools hatching of that left gap.

(1) Flat: the editor boxes (.ap-ed: stroke, stair) are a 1 px border on the card color; every input surface and handle plate gets the sunk screen look (.ap-ctl output: --screen + inset shadow) like the rest of the app. (2) Replace the 'wave · told' live scope (6 s trace of the commanded target, WAVE_MS) with a to-scale PLANNED MOTION strip under the stroke editor and above the rhythm section: the current parameters rendered over a fixed-length time window (default 10 s) on a 1 s grid, fully interpolated: trapezoidal halves per AdvancedPattern::halfStrokeSeconds (v = master x half x input ceiling, a = v^2/d x (1 + 9 knob)), dwells as flats in stroke periods, the rhythm modifier applied per stroke, so the user sees the final waveform rather than one stroke at a fixed editor width. title: Media clock ran away on WebKit: the hover time read 2:00 on a 37 s video and the scheduler ran off the end of the script
description: macOS WKWebView: the hover readout ran hours past a 37 s video, the preview flatlined, motion stopped. frameSource anchored the clock's wall side on rVFC expectedDisplayTime, which WebKit reports off the document time origin (operator read ~2.5 h, the time since wake). title: Fixed-height strip, compact top bar, rail swaps to the plan strip during motion
description:
Operator feedback 2026-10-02 (three annotated screenshots against valencesim). Build exactly:
1. NO PAGE SHIFTING. Top bar and strip fixed height. Errors, NACK refusals and the safety notice render in ONE status slot in the strip's center, overwriting by priority with a text reason; never a new line. The Pause-cleared banner line and the separate global refusal row are deleted.
2. ONE compact top bar, one row: left the heatmap mark and hub name; right the chips, then the window buttons (shell only). One live indicator (the phase chip); the second "live", the WS chip, the Menu handle and the shell row go. The bar is the Tauri drag region.
3. THE STRIP is the hero row: numerals left (hero, target, lag, speed); right one group: Halt-or-E-Stop and Pause (SafetyOp), Override/Return, Home (Force Home). Safety-reach holds at every viewport.
4. THE RAIL ROW under the strip, fixed height: the jog tape, replaced in place by PlanStrip while a source owns the rail (control-owner plus the pattern running role); swaps back on release.
5. Shell shading on the top bar (and, via ph-e82.16, the sidebar's Phosphor section); not on the strip or rail.

FINER CHOICES (each veto-able; record a ruling here to change one):
V1 Status slot priority: link fault > unattended > refusal > latch notice (halted / override / paused) > latest safety edge > idle (empty). Unattended outranks a refusal because RENDERING 10.1 rule 3 says moving-with-nobody-attached MUST be visible.
V2 The "no hub link" and "Link error" banners (LinkBar) moved into the slot as the fault class.
V3 A refusal stays until its remedy echoes OR the operator dismisses it with an x in the slot (new); it keys on lastRefusal.at, so a timeout fault with no NACK code now shows too.
V4 The numerals are rendered by TopStrip from RailWidget's published readout (getters over the rail's rAF state), so numeral and comet still share one instant. With no rail mounted the numeral area is empty and the strip keeps its height.
V5 Strip height depends on the viewport only: max(numeral block, --tap) + 12 px on one row at >= 760 px; at < 760 px two fixed rows (numerals + status, then the controls). Secondary numerals that do not fit wrap below and clip rather than grow the strip.
V6 Override/Return shows only while a rail is mounted (law 7, axis archetype); Home, Force Home and any other action.home / action.safety op render as one scrolling row after the pair; the e-stop/pause pair never scrolls.
V7 Flip stays on the rail: it rides the right end of the rail row.
V8 The jog tape's disabled reason renders inside its own label line ("jog . window . paused: press Override to jog"), not as a line under it; the inline "jog refused" echo is dropped (the slot shows the refusal).
V9 Rail owned = pattern running OR any control-owner slot held by a session other than this one; override latched shows the tape again (override is the one way to take the rail). A stream from this same session reads as unowned (ponytail, per-source once source ids are registry vocabulary).
V10 PlanStrip no longer collapses: inside the swap it always shows, dimming its lane when no plan is streaming.
V11 The two link dots and the decorative crosshair are deleted; the phase chip is the one live indicator, the rx chip carries telemetry health.
V12 The drag region is the top bar only (was the whole strip).
V13 TransportBar renders nothing (Home moved to the strip); App.svelte's three mounts are the sibling's to drop, then the file is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: safety-reach and responsive-matrix pass at every viewport; shell-chrome-geometry asserts bar height constant with and without a refusal, strip height constant with a long hub name and a long reason, rail row height constant across the swap; npm run check zero, npm test, npm run test:browser pass; Playwright against valencesim shows the swap and the refusal slot.
notes:
More finer choices (veto-able):
V14 Phone (< 760 px): two fixed grid rows, the primary numeral beside the status slot, the controls under them (a wrapping flex row once pushed the pair to a clipped third line; the grid makes that impossible). Watch size (<= 300 px): a current condition (fault, unattended, refusal, notice) covers the numeral cell; the edge history is left to the Log there.
V15 One-row shrink order: extra ops (Force Home, Clear Override, other device ops) scroll first, then the secondary numerals clip, then Override and Home scroll; the pair never shrinks. At >= 1440 px the numerals never shrink. The status slot reserves min(240 px, 25%) even idle, so nothing moves when it fills.
V16 The refusal's text is its own dismiss button (with an x glyph), beside "Fix: <op>" when the hub advertises the remedy; the refusal shows as "refused: CODE (label)", the detail in its title.
V17 The fault slot carries "Retry now" while the link is retrying or failed, so App's HubPicker mode=link row (which shifts the page ~50 px when the link drops) can go (sibling's call, comment on ph-e82.16).
V18 Bar: phase and tier chips are pinned; hub, catalog, render, rx shed first, then the name ellipsizes; under 400 px the heatmap (decor) goes first. Window buttons 40 px wide under 480 px. The rule under the bar is an inset shadow so the window buttons get the full bar height. Shell chip labels lift to --tx-val for 4.5:1.
V19 Close gate (operator request 2026-10-02): the X and every OS close request (onCloseRequested, preventDefault) open one popover under the X, out of flow (RENDERING 9 overlay), "Close Phosphor?" plus live consequences: background-run pattern keeps running > this session owns a source and it settles > the buttplug server is running (bp_status at open). One input: a 1 s press-and-hold (pointer or Enter/Space), intent-blue fill, never red; Esc or a click outside cancels and returns focus to the X. The hold destroys the window (close() would only re-raise the request), so src-tauri/capabilities/default.json gains core:window:allow-destroy (cargo check clean). With no event permission the gate degrades: the X still asks, an OS close goes through.
V20 Clipped chrome text must carry its full form in a title: the responsive matrix's clip check now skips text whose own or ancestor title contains it (the wordmark, the slot texts).

OWED: by-hand Tauri check of the close gate (X, Alt+F4, taskbar close, hold on a touch screen) and of the bar as the drag region; agents may not launch the window.

1. Edit toggle: ONE button, "Edit layout" / "Done" (aria-pressed), at the bar's right end. The layout picker is ALWAYS shown (switching layouts is a view choice, not an edit), so the active layout's name is on screen in and out of edit mode. Edit mode adds the cell lattice behind the grid and a one-line hint (grip moves, corner resizes, palette entries drag; arrows move, Shift+arrows resize; Ctrl+Z undoes). Handles stay edit-mode only (the rule stands).
2. Law 12: grab and resize handles are max(40 CSS px, --tap) at every scale step (at scale 0.67, --tap alone is 33 px). Asserted in responsive-matrix at 1280 and 0.67.
3. Drop target: a dashed intent-colored outline over the cells where the card lands, for pointer move/resize and palette drags. Not drawn when stacked (phone width keeps its live reorder). An empty grid keeps three cell rows in edit mode so it can take a drop.
4. Undo: ONE level over the whole layouts store (placements, nests, looks, layout save/rename/delete, module delete). Each synchronous burst of edits is one step (a palette add with a look is one step), recorded only if the store actually changed (a click on a grip never costs the real last change). Not undoable: layout switch, scale. Undo button plus Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z in edit mode unless a text control has focus.
5. Palette: sections stay collapsed until searched (as before); search also matches section and presentation names. Each field entry lists its offered presentations as chips (derived first); a chip adds the field with that look. An unplaced, placeable entry drags onto the grid (lands at the drop cell, fills to the row's end, at least 8 cells) or onto a nest (joins it unplaced, flows at its end). HTML5 drag: on touch, click-to-add stays the path.
6. Safety ops are TOP LEVEL ONLY (grid.js placeable('safety', inNest) false): a scrolling nest could carry a stop out of view (law 11), and the strip's copy is the one that cannot go. The palette tags them "Also in the strip" (red, --bad), "Strip and top level only" when a nest is the target, with Add disabled and the entry not draggable. title: Builder: top drawer and shell shading
description: Operator direction 2026-10-02: the shell gets a menu as a DRAWER AT THE TOP, and shell chrome is shaded darker so the boundary between shell chrome and hub-rendered content reads at a glance. Steps: (1) shell tokens --shell-bg/--shell-fg/--shell-border in style.css, applied to the shell row and drawer only; (2) src/shell/Drawer.svelte dropping from the shell row, panes Hubs (discovery + transport moved out of the row), Server (ServerPane as-is), Settings (registered via src/shell/drawer.js registerDrawerPane), About (hub identity, versions, UI build); row keeps handle, link state, window buttons; Escape and click outside close; in flow so it pushes the strip's safety pair down, never covers it (RENDERING 9, laws 1/11); open + pane remembered in localStorage; (3) phone width: full width, scrolls within itself, page scroll never trapped; (4) shell-chrome-geometry + responsive matrix + a11y. TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: npm run check zero, npm test, npm run test:browser; the geometry test builds the real shell bundle with a stubbed Tauri runtime and asserts the e-stop stays on screen with the drawer open at desktop and phone sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Drawer opens from the shell row; e-stop and pause visible and clickable with it open at 1440x900, 420x800 and a landscape phone; shell chrome visibly darker than content in default, light-ish themes and hi-vis with a11y contrast passing; npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser all pass.
notes:
VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (2026-10-02, agent):
1. Shading: --shell-bg = color-mix(--bg-sunken 40%, #000), --shell-fg = --ink, --shell-border = --line-3. PUSHBACK: the frozen chassis is already near black (--bg #08090B), so 'darker' has ~3% luminance headroom; the --line-3 rule under the shell carries most of the visible boundary. Lifting content surfaces instead would break the frozen-chassis rule. Measured: shell lum 0.0006 vs content 0.0027/0.0047; shell text worst 7.27:1 (default, hi-vis, prefers-contrast).
2. Desktop (>=960): the drawer is IN FLOW between the shell row and the LinkBar, so it pushes the e-stop/pause pair DOWN (operator's wording). max-height min(40dvh, 480px), scrolls within itself.
3. Phone (<960): the drawer opens BELOW THE WHOLE STRIP, over the content (position absolute in the sticky strip), so the e-stop never moves on a phone. Reason: in flow, the sticky strip grew past half a 568px screen and content under it failed the reach check. Content under the open drawer is covered by design; one --tap band stays uncovered to tap out.
4. Close on click, never pointerdown: closing moves the pair on desktop, and a control that moves between press and release loses the click (or the 3 s release hold). Tested: an e-stop click with the drawer open reaches the e-stop, then closes the drawer.
5. First run (no shell_drawer key and no shell_host) opens the drawer on Hubs, since discovery is the front door. Keys: shell_drawer ('1'/'0'), shell_drawer_pane.
6. Row keeps: Menu handle, WS/BLE chip, link phase, window buttons. The old collapse toggle is gone. Discovery, BLE scan, host entry (now with recent hubs, non-dense), the WS-upgrade button, notes and BLE wire counters moved to Hubs.
7. registerDrawerPane({id,label,component}) in src/shell/drawer.js (svelte/store writable, so late registration works): a built-in id (hubs/server/settings/about) replaces that pane; any other id adds a tab before About. Settings shows 'Nothing here yet.' until registered (settings-pane.js already registers id settings).
8. About: hub title (live identity.name, else WELCOME hub_name, else product), product, firmware, dialed endpoint, shell version (getVersion, '--' if denied), UI build.
9. Tabs follow WAI-ARIA: roving tabindex, ArrowLeft/Right, Home/End.
10. Shell window buttons and handle go to 40px under pointer: coarse (law 12).

title: RFC-085: override/return as one control on the rail's control row; jog replaces user in roles and labels
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 00:29 jog vocabulary, 00:39 mode merge, 00:42 final naming).

Change:
- override/return is an ESSENTIAL BINDING of the axis archetype: one two-state control on the rail widget's control row (beside home and Flip). Press = override (latches pause, hands the rail to the operator, lifts limits, enables jog); second press = return (smooth return to the paused position, then plain pause; no gate). A client with no rail control declines it and renders nothing (law 7); it is not a free-standing safety module. bypass and override_on/off controls retire; the per-move bypass key is not sent (follow the landed text).
- Jog (tap-to-move) is offered only under override; outside override a jog is refused by the hub (SOURCE_CONFLICT) while a source owns the rail, and the rail shows that refusal. Window edits stay live at all times.
- 'jog' replaces 'user' in roles and labels: src/model/roles.js limitUserSpeed/limitUserAccel ('limit.user.speed'/'limit.user.accel') follow the landed registry names; any UI copy saying user speed.

Likely files: src/ui/hero/RailWidget.svelte, src/model/roles.js, src/model/actions.js (HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS override_on/bypass_on), src/ui/TransportBar.svelte, docs/DESIGN.md. Consumes Valence rfc-q93.

Prove it: unit test: rail declines override/return when the role is absent, binds when present; live smoke against valencesim: tap-to-move under a stream refused, override then jog accepted outside limits, return lands at the paused position; npm run check zero findings.
close_reason: Device-free complete (see the 2026-10-02 comment for commit, decisions, verification); live checks owed on ph-vdk.55

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02 landed in 0f6f56f (roles rename in 4b5f99f). Decisions (VETO-ABLE):

1. Override/Return is SafetyOp with op = override, rendered in RailWidget's hero row (.rw-hero-accessory) before Flip and the Home accessory. No rail, no control; a hub whose safety-intents op table lacks override, no control (law 7).
2. Override is confirm-gated (actions.js HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS = {override}: it lifts the window and soft limits); Return takes no gate (law 14). Confirm copy is client text describing SPEC §11.1.
3. PUSHBACK, flagged: the task text said "jog enabled only while override is latched". Landed SPEC §11.4 (RFC-085 open question 2, answered at landing) says a manual point move on an idle, unpaused, unowned rail is an ordinary source activation, so gating the tape to override-only would take away a move the hub accepts. Coded the hub's gate instead: e-stop latched -> disabled "e-stop latched: no motion until release"; paused without override -> disabled "paused: press Override to jog" (hub: INTERLOCK); override -> enabled over the whole travel ("jog · travel"); idle and unpaused -> enabled over the window. A source owning the rail is the hub's SOURCE_CONFLICT, shown as "jog refused: SOURCE_CONFLICT (a source owns the rail: press Override to jog)". Veto to make it override-only and I flip one derived.
4. Jog naming: limit.jog.speed/accel (Jog speed/accel), the Limits widget's "Jog limits", the tape's mode label and aria-label. The tape's CSS class names are unchanged (probes key on them). No per-move bypass key was ever sent from the rail.

Verified device-free: check:safety ALL PASS (decline with no rail and with an op table cut before override, rail still present in the latter; one control beside Home; paused reason; confirm with nothing sent before it; Override -> Return -> Override on the wire as 7, 8; tape domain switches to travel); npm run check zero, npm test green.
OWED live (valencesim once it speaks RFC-085): tap-to-move under a stream refused, override then jog accepted outside limits, return lands at the paused position.

title: RFC-085: TCode and buttplug adapters RESUME explicitly; no motion intent clears pause
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn) description item 4 and ruling 2026-10-01: Phosphor's TCode and buttplug adapters RESUME EXPLICITLY. Under the fold no motion intent clears PAUSE (RESUME is the only clear; RFC-074 under RFC-085 drops stream bundles while paused and counts them).

Change: the adapters (src/model/motion.js TCode path, src/plugins/buttplug.js, src/shell/bp-server.js) never assume a motion intent or a STREAM bundle re-arms the machine. When paused, incoming motion is refused locally with a visible 'machine paused' reason (no silent drops), and resume is an explicit act (the strip control, or an adapter command the operator maps), sent as RESUME; StopCmd/stopAll keep their current meaning for toys and map to PAUSE for the machine only if the ruling's adapter text says so (state the choice here). The bp-server 'stop sends nothing' comment and buttplug.js header are rewritten to the new model.

Prove it: test/buttplug-bridge.test.mjs and a TCode adapter test: motion while paused is refused with a reason and nothing reaches the wire; after RESUME motion flows; test/buttplug-estop-sim.mjs still passes.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02 landed in 00883fa. Decisions (VETO-ABLE):

1. One guard where every adapter routes: motion.js createMotionDoor takes an optional halted() dep; shadow.svelte.js wires it to the REPORTED latch (machine.safety): "paused, resume to continue", or "e-stop latched, release and resume to continue". While it returns a reason every input is refused with it and nothing is published or set. This is a mirror of the hub's latch, not a second policy: the hub still drops (and counts) the bundles itself.
2. Neither adapter, nor the door, has a resume path. Resume is only the operator's strip Resume. No plugin API addition for an adapter-mapped resume (RFC-085's "send resume explicitly" read as: only an explicit operator act sends it).
3. StopCmd/stopAll keep their meaning (submit nothing; toys stop); they never map to PAUSE. DESIGN §10.8's ruling stands.
4. The TCode adapter and buttplug bridge already log one line per refusal reason and count refusals (TCode shows it on its settings line); their headers state the never-re-arm constraint. docs/BUTTPLUG.md Stop and Pause/e-stop rewritten.
5. test/buttplug-estop-sim.mjs builds its door WITHOUT halted, so it still proves the hub latch alone stops a live stream. Ran it against valencesim: all passed (estop op 6 is unchanged).

Verified: plugins.test (e) and buttplug-bridge.test (e) (three bp://motion payloads and two TCode lines through the real host: one log line each, nothing on the wire, both flow after the latch clears); npm run check zero, npm test green. title: RFC-085: top strip pair becomes pause/resume and estop/release, one control each; hold-to-release; Halt label when estop_cuts_power is false
description:
RFC-085 (Valence rfc-crn), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 00:42 final naming and control shape, 00:47 ESTOP behavior, 00:48 machines without a motor switch, 00:49 declaration duty).

Change (RENDERING law 1 follows):
- The persistent strip's mandatory pair is e-stop plus pause. EACH PAIR IS ONE CONTROL WITH TWO STATES: no separate clear/release/resume button anywhere. STOP and HOLD buttons and every clear button retire.
- Pause: press latches PAUSE (any tier, role-exempt), second press is RESUME (no gate).
- E-stop: press latches; the latched state reads 'Halted'; release is PRESS-AND-HOLD on the same control, 3 s (RENDERING SHOULD, every renderer class), so two panic taps never latch-then-release; the hub still answers CLEAR_REFUSED and the strip shows it. After release on a power-cutting hub the strip shows paused + home required (resume refused while unhomed).
- Label: a hub that declared estop_cuts_power TRUE renders 'E-Stop'; FALSE or ABSENT renders 'Halt' (Clients MUST NOT render E-Stop on a hub that declared false; absent = false).
- Refusal mapping (shadow.svelte.js NACK.ESTOP_ACTIVE -> estop_clear) follows the release rename.

Likely files: src/ui/TopStrip.svelte, src/ui/TransportBar.svelte, src/model/actions.js (HAZARD_SAFETY_OPS), src/model/shadow.svelte.js, src/model/machine.svelte.js (safety word decode, one PAUSE bit), docs/DESIGN.md strip section. Coordinates with ph-e82.2 (strip in progress). Consumes Valence rfc-q93 at the pin bump.

Prove it: test/safety-reach.test.mjs and responsive-matrix assert exactly one e-stop and one pause control in the strip at every viewport; a fixture with estop_cuts_power false asserts the label is 'Halt' (H1 made testable, named by the 00:48 ruling); a fixture with it absent asserts 'Halt'; a hold shorter than 3 s sends nothing; live smoke against valencesim: pause, resume, estop, hold-release.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02 landed in 4fc3571 (vocabulary groundwork 4b5f99f). Decisions (VETO-ABLE):

1. One component, src/ui/widgets/SafetyOp.svelte, is every safety pair (law 14): the strip's two fixed controls, the placed copies, and (ph-vdk.41) the rail's override/return. State is the hub's latch only: session.js decodeSafetySnapshot of 0x0003 (registry bits), mirrored as machine.safety; a control never flips on its own press.
2. E-stop: tap latches; latched reads Halted with hint "hold 3 s to release"; release is the same control held 3000 ms (pointer, or Enter/Space held); a shorter hold and any tap on Halted send nothing. The click that ends a completed hold is judged on the latch at PRESS START, so it can never re-latch the e-stop (a real bug found while testing: without the guard the mouseup click after release re-sent estop). A bottom bar fills over the 3 s; reduced motion drops the animation, the text "keep holding to release" stays.
3. Label: identity.estop_cuts_power === true renders E-Stop, else Halt (machine.svelte.js estopLabel()); hint "cut power" vs "stop motion".
4. Pause: tap sends pause; latched reads Resume ("paused", or "home required" when modes bit1 is set); tap sends resume, no gate. Unknown state (no snapshot yet) shows the latching op, the safe default.
5. Strip: bound to the spec-core safety-intents action alone (law 2). That channel now draws NO other op buttons in the strip (release/resume are second states, override/return are the rail's). The ESTOP_ACTIVE -> estop_clear remedy button is deleted (it was a separate release button); NOT_HOMED -> Home stays.
6. TransportBar is Home only (its pause/stop/e-stop copies deleted). Placeable safety modules are safety:estop and safety:pause; saved safety:stop/hold/estop_clear placements stay inert (law 10).
7. DashItem reserves the resize handle's height in edit mode (the shorter pair module put its Remove under the handle).

Verified device-free: npm run check zero, npm test green; check:safety ALL PASS (exactly one e-stop and one pause in the strip at 360x800, 844x390, 1280x720, 1920x1080, mouse and touch, hero and no-hero; Halt for WELCOME without key 6 and with false, E-Stop with true; pause -> Resume -> resume; latch -> Halted; two taps and a 1 s hold send nothing; a 3.3 s hold sends release once and lands in pause, mouse and touch), check:responsive, check:contract, check:home, check:nest, check:shell, check:dash ALL PASS.

title: controlKey gives uid keys for role fields in the running app (proxy identity)
description: settings.js controlKey() picks the role key only when byRole.get(role)[0] === f. In the app, machine is deep $state, so model.fields[i] reaches placeableControls as a Svelte proxy while model.byRole (a Map, never proxied) holds the raw object: the identity check always fails and every role field is keyed uid:<ch>:<name> (live valencesim: uid:4608:running for pattern.running). Node tests (settings-model) see raw objects and pass, so the suite cannot catch it. Law 10 prefers the role key; persisted home and nest keys are being written as uids today. Fix: compare uids (first[0].uid === f.uid) in controlKey, plus a test that keys the model through $state or compares against byRole by uid. test/home.test.mjs normalizes keys to uids (keyUid) and needs no change after the fix. Saved layouts already holding uid keys for role fields will go inert on the fix unless the lookup accepts both; decide before fixing.

title: ActionField payload inputs ignore the secret flag: a passphrase payload renders in plain text
description:
RFC-009.4 / SPEC §8.8 'Secrets (normative)': a secret-flagged field's value is never shown. Field.svelte honors flagBits.secret (WIDGET.secret, type=password), but src/ui/ActionField.svelte renders every tstr payload input as type=text, and settings.js pass 2 drops flagBits when it builds an action's payload list. A wifi_join passphrase typed into an action is therefore on screen in clear text. Found by the provisioning wizard agent.

title: Builder (d): home page replaces Overview; palette and edit mode
description:
Phase (d), DESIGN §10.1. The home page replaces Overview (App.svelte tab {id: 'machine', label: 'Overview'} and machineItems). Everything that lived only on Overview becomes a module (hero-rank leftovers, telemetry, card-zone heroes, loose actions) or is deleted with C-9 proof. Default home when the user has none: seeded from rank (RENDERING §4 hero surfaced, ph-vdk.36) plus the migrated Default layout from (b). Edit mode: a palette listing every placeable control (fields by category, composites, plugin widgets, safety modules); place, move, resize, delete; outside edit mode nothing is draggable (the DashItem grab-handle rule stands). Derived category pages stay and keep every field reachable (§12). Full class only until the mobile ruling (f).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- Playwright on the fake-hub harness: no Overview tab; every field Overview showed is reachable from home or its category page (diff against a list captured from the tree before the change); the palette lists every fixture-catalog field exactly once plus every claimed composite; edit mode toggles drag handles; a write in flight survives entering and leaving edit mode.

title: Builder (b): physical-pixel square grid, scale control, named layouts store, migration of per-class dash layouts
description:
Phase (b), DESIGN §10.5 and §10.6 (layouts half). Replace the 12-column span model (dashboard.svelte.js DEFAULT_SPAN/MAX_SPAN, DashItem.svelte colPx) with square cells sized in device pixels: cell edge in CSS px = device px / devicePixelRatio, default in the 32 to 40 device px band measured at 3840x2160 at 125 percent. Cell count follows the window. A browser-style scale control multiplies the cell edge. Items carry {x, y, w, h} in cells. Scale is done by cell size and tokens, never CSS zoom on a subtree holding a positional control, until a test proves RailWidget's clientX mapping survives (ph-gf8's concern). Under a coarse pointer the scale clamps so no hit target drops under the 40 CSS px floor (law 12). Layout store: named layouts, per client, localStorage with the existing try/catch degrade; keyed on stable ids (law 10); absent ids stay inert. Migration: today's phosphor.dash.<cls>.<viewId> maps and the legacy sd32.dash.* keys seed a layout named Default; legacy keys are read, never written or deleted. rclass.js class selection stays in CSS px, unaffected.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN (all device-free):
- New node suite test/grid-model.test.mjs (added to npm run check): device-px to CSS-px conversion at DPR 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2; cell count per window width; scale clamp under coarse pointer; save, rename, delete, switch named layouts; absent ids stay inert and survive a round trip; storage throwing degrades to in-memory; migration from a seeded 12-span map and from a legacy sd32 key keeps visual order and never writes the legacy key.
- test/dash-measure.test.mjs extended: measured cell edge in device px equals the target at deviceScaleFactor 1.25 and 2.
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs: no horizontal page scroll at any scale step; target floor holds at the smallest scale on phone viewports.
acceptance_criteria: DashGrid places {x,y,w,h} items on device-px square cells with a scale control; named layouts save, switch and survive reload; existing layouts migrate to Default with order kept; grid-model suite in npm run check.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-01 decisions (veto-able, recorded per autonomy bar):
1. Scale is browser-style for the whole client: the step sets the --s token on <html> (rem, --tap, thumbs) and multiplies the cell edge. No CSS zoom anywhere (ph-gf8 RailWidget concern untouched).
2. Coarse pointer: scale never goes below 1. A --tap-derived floor (0.9 allowed) was tried and the matrix failed: chip-num inputs are rem-sized at ~42 CSS px and drop to 38 at 0.9. Floor proven at 1 only.
3. Max scale per window: a step is offered only while viewport/scale >= 320 CSS px (the narrowest laid-out viewport). 360 px phone gets 1 and 1.1.
4. Default card width 48 cells = 12 old spans x 4 (a full 1920 DPR1 pane); migration maps span s to 4s cells. Consequence: on DPR 2 (retina 1440) a default card is 864 CSS px, not full width; at 3840x2160@125% two cards sit side by side. Alternative if vetoed: unsaved items fill the row.
5. Rows are minmax(cell, auto): h is a floor; a card whose content is taller grows its rows, never clips a control. Items stretch to fill their area so a resize in cells is visible.
6. Vertical compaction: saved items keep their column and rise to the first free row; a drag pins the dragged item and everything else yields. Keyboard: Up/Down swap reading order, Left/Right step one cell, Shift+arrows resize.
7. Viewports <= 640 CSS px stack full width as before (mobile is ph-e82.7); a stacked drag commits a reading order, never cells.
8. Store: localStorage phosphor.layouts = {active, layouts: {name: {'<cls>.<viewId>': {id: {x,y,w,h}}}}}; one map per (renderer class, view) inside each named layout. phosphor.scale holds the wished step. phosphor.dash.* and sd32.dash.* are read to seed Default and never written or deleted; the store is written only on a user change.
9. Layout UI is minimal and lives in DashGrid's edit-mode toolbar (select, name field, Save as, Rename, Delete); the scale control (- 100% +) is always shown. ph-e82.5 owns the real palette and edit mode.

title: Builder (c): control contract: field + presentation registry from archetypes, resize and aspect orientation, composites and plugin widgets under it
description:
Phase (c), DESIGN §10.2. A control is one catalog field plus a presentation chosen from the set its archetype allows. Presentation registry keyed by archetype code, grown from settings.js resolveArchetype/resolveWidget and WIDGET; rendered by Field.svelte. The offered set is filtered by the field's facts: bar needs bounds, toggle and bulb need a bool, graph needs a client-side history ring (missing samples are gaps, law 9). The user picks how it looks, never what it binds (laws 6, 7). Every presentation keeps the universal contract: four-state ladder with text reason (law 5), graying with the gate named (law 3), stale dim (law 8), echo pair co-located and range pairs as one control (§11, mergeRangePairs). Resize: each control declares minimum cells per orientation; orientation follows its own aspect (w >= h horizontal). Role-claiming composites (heroes.js rail, pattern, limits; PlanStrip stays nested in the rail per §10 plan-view) are controls under the same placement, size and save rules; claimAll (roles.js) claim-or-decline is unchanged. Plugin heroes (host.js registerHero, zone card) become placeable controls under the same contract. Safety ops become placeable modules; the strip's mandatory e-stop is not one of them. Absorbs ph-vdk.22's placement question (a tuning composite is one more role-claiming control).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- test/settings-model.test.mjs: for every field in the fixture catalog, the offered presentation set is non-empty, contains the derived default, and never offers bar without bounds or toggle for a non-bool.
- test/plugins.test.mjs: a plugin hero is placeable, resizable and persisted under hero:plugin:<name>:<id>; a throwing plugin hero drops to generic fields as today.
- New Playwright suite test/control-contract.test.mjs on the fake-hub harness (responsive-matrix.mjs pattern): each presentation of one writable field shows pending then confirmed on a synthetic echo, overdue past the timeout, fault on a NACK, with the text reason; an aspect flip at w = h swaps orientation without dropping an in-flight write.
- Live against valencesim (test/actions-live.test.mjs pattern): one slider-class field driven through knob, slider and stepper, each confirmed on a second raw session (C-8).
- npm run check (device-knowledge gate) stays green.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalog field is placeable with a presentation from its allowed set; composites and plugin heroes place, resize and persist the same way; every presentation passes the four-state ladder suite; one field verified live on valencesim in three presentations.

title: Builder rulings owed: user-built home vs RENDERING §9/§11, cross-archetype presentation, law-10 keys, single fields vs nests
description:
Rulings the builder needs before the control contract (c) and the home page (d) are coded. DESIGN §10.1, §10.2. Each is a RENDERING conflict or an open product question; none is resolved in code.

1. User-built home vs derivation. RENDERING §11 "pages are derived from the catalog, never designed per app", §9 "a pattern's region assignment is part of its spec definition, never a per-app choice", and the §11 consistency invariant, against a user-arranged home where composites go wherever the user drops them. Proposed read: the home is an ADDITIONAL user surface; the derived category pages stay and keep every field reachable (§12), so the invariant holds for the derived tree. Needs an operator ruling and, if accepted, a Valence RFC stating a user-authored surface is conformant (never code against an unaccepted clause).
2. Presentation across archetypes. Knob, bar, segmented are projections inside one archetype (settings.js WIDGET already has such variants). slider vs stepper (§8.2 rows 9/10) and readout vs graph (rows 12/13 vs row 15) cross an archetype boundary that §8.2 decides by the first matching row. Ruling: allow as a user override (RFC), or restrict the offered set to the derived archetype's projections.
3. Law 10 keys. A single-field control with no role has only its uid (channel id + field name) as a stable key, which is wire vocabulary. Ruling: accept uid (inert when absent, the dashboard.svelte.js rule) or require a role for placement outside the derived pages.
4. Single fields placeable anywhere vs only inside nests (operator: undecided).

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: none (decision). Each ruling is recorded as a dated comment here, then written into DESIGN §10 with an amendments row in the same commit; RFCs filed in Valence RFC-QUEUE where item 1 or 2 is accepted.
acceptance_criteria: Four rulings recorded as dated comments and written into DESIGN §10; any accepted RENDERING change filed as a Valence RFC.

title: Builder (a): top strip replaces OS decorations, ShellBar and the bottom safety dock; mandatory e-stop; full width

Live-verified against Nucleus 631f31d valencesim (42-entry catalog, pattern plane present), test/actions-live.test.mjs, commit 1e0f008. Both viewports (390x844 touch, 1280x800 mouse).

PASS [verified 2026-09-25 -- node test/actions-live.test.mjs against valencesim --homed --port 8882 --http 8880]:
- Actions card renders the pattern-presets-cmd action.preset trigger (save/load/delete/rename, only non-persistent action.* this catalog advertises; no has_drive machine-admin here)

LEFT OPEN, two related findings (both documented inline in the test with wire evidence, not silently weakened):
1. A pattern-presets-cmd SAVE sent from the browser gets a well-formed ECHO from the hub (captured via CDP framereceived, decoded FRAME.ECHO ch=0x3220 applied={1:1,2:slot,3:name} within ms) but the ActionField shadow never leaves 'pending' -- session.sendIntent's promise never resolves. The identical payload from a plain Node session (with or without a real /uitoken token, with light or heavy subscription load) gets its echo in ~10-15ms. Reproduces only inside a browser runtime. Suspect Valence/clients/js/session.js's echo/intent correlation, not ActionField or runAction (both are straight pass-throughs).
2. Loading the saved slot does not actually recall the saved value (checked via 0x1210 master, an ordinary captured field) even though load's own confirmed-text arrives normally. Roster count mechanics (create/destroy the slot) work correctly on both save and delete. Likely the same root cause as (1) rather than a second bug.

Neither looks like a Phosphor UI defect -- everything Phosphor itself renders and drives matches the wire. Recommend a follow-up bead against the Valence client library once triaged there.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSES (both findings closed, commit 831ca60).
1. Save never confirmed: NOT the Valence library. src/model/shadow.svelte.js ensureShadow did `sh = shadows[k] = {...}`; the assignment expression yields the RAW object, not the $state proxy, so every transition on the FIRST write to a shadow key bypassed Svelte signals (settle after the ECHO, and writeSetting/sendCommand overdue/fail timers). CDP capture showed INTENT seq=1 intent_id=1 and ECHO intent_id=1 correlating correctly; the promise resolved, the UI just never saw it. Load worked only because save had already created the record. Fix: assign, then read back through shadows[k].
2. Load did not recall master: test assumption. Nucleus flagship_p4/src/patterns/PatternSettings.h capturePreset() snapshots in/out speed, in/out accel and modifier lanes, never master; reproduced identically from plain Node. Marker switched to in_speed (0x3210 key 5).

title: Generic readouts never dim on staleness; telemetry chart fabricates a held line (laws 8, 9, T18)
description:
MISSING: only the rail hero and hero numerals dim stale values. Field readouts ignore sampleTs and the link phase, so after a link drop every generic card keeps showing the last value at full contrast. TelemetryChart samples the retained snapshot every animation frame and stamps it with performance.now(), so a dead link draws a flat, confident line instead of a gap, and a clumped burst is re-timed to render time (T18). Its default roles are position and velocity only, so the power/current/temperature lanes its header promises are never drawn.

title: Scrub overshoots when the pointer stops after a fast move
description: Operator 2026-10-05: scrubbing the tape and stopping abruptly after a fast move overshoots the final position, then corrects. Two candidate causes, bench both. Client (RailWidget onTapePointerMove -> requestMove): jogs are coalesced at the move channel's catalog max rate, so the last pointer samples collapse into one move whose implied velocity is the fast run's; also pointer events arrive at the mouse's own rate (125 Hz to 1 kHz), not frame rate. Hub (Nucleus chase planner, kinetic_tuning chase_aim_extrap / chase_lookahead / chase_ff): a jog stream that stops dead is extrapolated past the final target. Measure: log the jog values sent with hub-time stamps against telemetry.position, find where the extra travel is born. Sibling: val-vw2n (hub side).

title: Factory plugin: funscript player with Stash support
description:
Factory widget plugin plugins/factory/funscript-player: plays a local or Stash video and drives the rail from its L0 funscript. Design: docs/plugins/FUNSCRIPT.md. Builder contract: plugins/factory/funscript-player/CONTRACT.md. Synthesized from three designs (sync, ux, protocol) by the judge, 2026-10-03.

SUMMARY
Media is the master clock: requestVideoFrameCallback presentation times map media time to performance.now() (median filter, 5 ms/s slew, 40 ms step re-anchor; currentTime fallback). The scheduler turns each funscript span into one segment {atMs execution start, norm, durationMs}, tiled from one mapping and sent once. It reaches the machine through ONE new host member, api.submitSegments(list): the host converts to hub time, subtracts the grant's schedule_latency_us (RFC-059), clips a late start keeping its end, takes what starts within HALF the granted horizon (RFC-087 keeps the RFC-014 SHOULD; registry max_future_schedule_ms note), packs 100 us t_off, and publishes on the segments STREAM found by role (0x2101 on valencesim, never named in code). Seek, rate, offset and transform changes are new superseding bundles (RFC-087 item 5); a stop is a short hold segment ending at rest, never PAUSE. Content goes as authored: end velocity unspecified, no curve_family, no client feasibility (SPEC 9.6 clauses 2, 4, 5). Safety gates ride the existing api.gate(field), extended to the c2h motion-input field: link, tier, latch, generator running, rail owned by another session, another plugin producing. Never auto-resumes. The card is a DAW-style arrangement: video stage, overview heat with scrub, an automation detail view (intent curve, measured reality trace), a fixed transport (Play, time, Motion, Offset, Invert, speed meter, volume) and one status slot; nothing shifts. Stash rides api.net.fetch (shell tauri-plugin-http) with GraphQL findScenes; every Stash fact is a marked assumption.

DECISIONS (veto-able; full reasons in FUNSCRIPT.md)
D1 Segments only, one new host door; the hero requires input.target + input.duration and declines elsewhere. No samples fallback.
D2 Lookahead = half the granted horizon, enforced in the host. The player offers up to 32; the host returns how many it consumed.
D3 The host owns time: atMs is an absolute performance.now() execution start; stamp = exec - schedule_latency_us. submitMotion's now+latency stamp is flagged for its owner, not changed here.
D4 As authored: end velocity unspecified, no curve_family. Stop-start at same-direction knots, if the live test shows it, is a Nucleus bead; client PCHIP end velocities are the veto alternative.
D5 rVFC media clock with median, slew and step (design 1).
D6 One mapping, segments tile, each sent once; restart supersedes.
D7 Stop = hold along the script min(200 ms, next action), at rest. Preroll on Play when the machine sits more than 5 % of the stroke from the script.
D8 Gates via api.gate on the segments field; a gate mid-play pauses the video; never auto-resume.
D9 One motion producer per session (host lock until the last sent segment ends + 500 ms).
D10 Offset (+-500 ms, 5 ms; zero = declared latency), Range (share of the hub window) and Invert are client content transforms; the window is never written; no intent permission.
D11 Speed meter and heat against limit.input.speed are display only.
D12 Dense scripts are thinned only after RATE_EXCEEDED, at the grant rate, extrema kept.
D13 Stash: direct stream only, Boolean interactive filter (assumption A3), no transcodes in v1.
D17 PUSHING BACK on the computed task: permissions are motion + net.fetch, not intent (the player writes no field); the manifest gets no panes key (the schema has none).
D18 Hub clock-offset filtering is deferred to a measurement on the P4; a fix belongs in Valence clients/js syncClock.
D19 No releaseMotion: PUBLISH rate 0 does not release the source (measured on valencesim).

OPERATOR RULINGS NEEDED BEFORE THE HOST LANDS THEM
R-A CANON FLAG: api.net.fetch (permission net.fetch) against DESIGN 2 'no HTTP backdoors'. Refuses the hub's own origins. No Stash without it.
R-B CSP: media-src 'self' blob: http: https: (blob: alone is needed for local files), img-src + http: https:; http capability + https://**.
R-C CANON FLAG: multi-module factory plugin against PLUGINS.md 'manifest plus one module'; an override copy must be bundled into one file.
R-D Permissions: motion + net.fetch, no intent (pushback above).

PROTOCOL GAPS (Valence RFC drafts owed, not built)
G1 A stream source stays owned until the session ends; no release intent is registered (SPEC 11.4 names one). Measured: jog refused SOURCE_CONFLICT after playback; PUBLISH rate 0 releases nothing.
G2 Stream vs generator exclusion is not enforced on Nucleus (an Advanced start and a segments bundle were both accepted, design 2 measurement); the player self-gates on pattern.running / advgen.running.

title: Phone strip is 55 px shorter with the link down: one row instead of two, the page jumps
description: At 390x844 the top strip measures 160 px with a live hub (stacked: numeral and status row over a controls row) and 105 px when the link is down or the hub is absent (single row: status, Retry, Pause, Halt), so every reconnect or drop moves the whole page ~55 px. Cause: the measured budget in TopStrip measure() drops to one row when Home, Flip and Override are absent (no catalog, no ops), so stacked flips with link state. title: Layout switching: no position transitions, unsaved-changes prompt before switch, JSON export/import from the Layout menu
close_reason: Landed c3d52e9; decisions (incl. the autosave pushback) veto-able in the comment; builder-edit layouts + grid-model export green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed c3d52e9. VETO-ABLE: (1) PUSHBACK, recorded: layouts autosave on every edit (since ph-e82.3), so there are no literally unsaved changes and a plain 'unsaved changes?' prompt would be noise. The guard instead asks about changes SINCE EDITING BEGAN (or since the layout became active while editing): switching then shows an inline bar, not a modal (layout is not a hazard; ConfirmLayer stays for hazard prompts): Keep and switch / Discard and switch / Stay. Discard puts the layout back to that baseline (one undo step). Outside edit mode a switch never asks (the only writes there are nest folds). If you want explicit-save semantics instead (edits staged until Save), that is a larger change: say so. (2) No motion: the grid has no transition or animation on position, size or reflow, and the test asserts document.getAnimations() and transition-duration are empty/zero on the grid right after a switch (webui.md has no position-animation rule; law 12 reduced motion and 'nothing that could mislead' are the reasons). The dragged card's lift is a static offset. (3) Export/import live in the Layout menu (edit mode), shaped like the SettingsPane prefs backup: a textarea plus Export (fills it and copies to the clipboard) and Import. JSON is {app: 'phosphor', layout: name, views: {'<class>.<view>': placement map}}; modules are NOT included (a nest carries its own members). Import validates, keeps only object maps keyed class.view, never overwrites (a taken name becomes 'Name 2', 'Name 3'), a missing or prototype name becomes 'Imported', and refusals are named in words. Import then switches to it through the same guard. The prefs backup already carries phosphor.layouts whole, so the two stay consistent. Evidence: grid-model export block; builder-edit layouts block (guard bar, Stay keeps the change, Discard restores and switches, no animation or transition, a clean switch goes at once, Export JSON, Import as Default 2 and switched, foreign text refused). Toggled by a 'Compact cards in <layout>' switch in the Layout menu; it is an edit like any other (undoable, and it counts as a change for the switch guard). title: Multi-select in edit mode (shift-click, marquee): group move and delete, duplicate a card or nest, align and distribute
close_reason: Landed fd71c66; decisions veto-able in the comment; builder-edit select + grid-model selection green

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed fd71c66. VETO-ABLE: (1) Selecting: a click on a card's GRIP selects it alone (a second click clears), Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click adds or drops; keyboard Space on a focused grip does the same (aria-pressed carries the state). A click after a real drag is not a selection. A pointer drag across EMPTY grid draws a marquee and selects every card it crosses (Shift adds); a click on empty grid clears. Fine pointer only: no touch-action change, so a touch on empty grid still scrolls the page. Selection is per grid (a nest's members select within the nest), edit mode only, cleared on Done. (2) The edit hint line is replaced by a selection bar while anything is selected (no layout shift beyond the hint's own row): N selected, Duplicate, Align left, Align top (2+), Spread (3+), Remove, Clear. The toolbar keeps one row. (3) Group move: dragging a selected card's grip moves the whole selection by the same cell delta, clamped as one at the grid edges; a group never joins or leaves a nest by drag (single cards only). (4) Align left/top move every selected card to the selection's smallest x/y; Spread keeps the outermost two and spaces the rest evenly in x order. Collisions resolve by pushing the later card down, never by overlap. (5) Duplicate: a NEST is copied whole (members, their places and looks) under the next nest id, titled '<title> copy', placed below. A CARD on the home becomes a second placement keyed '<key>#<n>' (n from 2), same control, own place and own look; the palette still counts the control once and its Remove takes every placement, while the card's own Remove and the group Remove take only that placement. Law 10 reading: the instance key is the stable id plus a user-made instance number, never an index into catalog order, and it never binds anything new. Category pages and nest members offer no card Duplicate (a control is placed once per map); Duplicate is disabled there with a tooltip. (6) Remove on the home deletes from the home (a nest with its members, except members another nest also holds); on a category page it ungroups a nest; inside a nest it steps the member out. One undo step for the group. Owed elsewhere: Field.svelte uses field.uid as the element id, so two placements of one control (Duplicate, or one control in two nests, possible since ph-e82.6) give duplicate DOM ids; filed separately (not this agent's file). Evidence: grid-model selection block; builder-edit select block (grip click + Shift, group drag, marquee, align left without overlap, nest and card duplicate, group remove keeping a shared member, one undo, Done clears); home, nest, a11y, responsive home+nest green.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed 0a9ed08. VETO-ABLE: (1) Collapse is a layout property (nest.collapsed in the stored nest, per layout and view), toggled by a chevron at the start of the nest bar that is there in and out of edit mode. A collapsed nest packs NEST_FOLD_H = 2 rows (its card head plus the bar; rows still grow to content) and keeps its stored height for the unfold; things below rise. Members are unmounted while collapsed (their write state lives in the model, so nothing is lost). (2) Law 9 invariant: collapsing hides the members, NEVER the bar: the in-flight count stays drawn (nest.test asserts it on a held write). (3) The header IS the card head: in edit mode a nest's title is an inline input there (Enter or blur commits, Escape restores, an empty name is refused); the bar's separate name input is gone. (4) The bar holds, in order: fold, member count, in-flight count, then in edit mode: inert count, Add, Scrolling/Fixed (aria-pressed), Save module, Ungroup. Save module saves under the nest's title; a taken name is refused with 'rename the nest first' (no overwrite, no prompt). (5) Empty nest: 'Drop controls here' in edit mode, 'Empty nest' otherwise, drawn over the subgrid without taking its pointer events. (6) Module reinsert: choosing a module in the Layout menu previews its members before Insert: titled when this view can draw them, else the stored key marked '(not available here)', plus 'N of M available here; the rest stay inert until a catalog has them'. Insert is the confirmation and announces the same count. On the home 'available' means the catalog has it (Home resolves through its module list); on a category page it means the page draws it. title: Keyboard: arrow nudge, shift-arrow resize, reading-order Tab, Enter opens the look picker, Delete removes, Escape cancels a drag

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed 6db3fc6. VETO-ABLE: (1) Up/Down CHANGED meaning on the grid: they used to swap reading order (commitOrder, which could fling a card across columns); they now pass the nearest card above/below in the card's own columns (grid.js nudgePin), because with vertical compaction a one-cell vertical step is always undone. At the top/bottom of its columns nothing moves and the live region says so. Left/Right step one cell, clamped. Stacked (phone width) Up/Down still walk the reading order. Keyboard moves act on the focused card only, never the group (group move is pointer-only for now). (2) Focus stays on the moved grip: a keyed #each reorder drops focus from the moved node, so it is restored after the move. (3) Tab order = DOM order = reading order (y, then x); during a pointer drag the DOM order is frozen (from ph-e82.20.2) and resyncs on release. (4) Enter on a grip opens the card's presentation picker: Home wraps LookEditor in [data-look]; the grid focuses that select and calls showPicker() where it exists. A card with no choices says so. Enter no longer clicks the grip (Space still selects). (5) Delete or Backspace on a grip removes the card, or its whole selection when it is selected; Ctrl+Z restores. (6) Escape: a drag in flight (pointer move/resize, marquee, a member leaving its nest) is dropped with nothing written; otherwise, outside text fields and popovers, it clears the selection. title: Drag feedback: lifted card, live sibling reflow, drop rect, nest highlight on drop, drag a member out of a nest to the top level

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed eec589f. VETO-ABLE: (1) The drag preview is the COMPACTED result (grid.js settle, shared with commitPin): the dragged card and its siblings are drawn where the release leaves them, so dragging into empty space below shows the card risen to where gravity puts it, not under the pointer. Honest over literal. (2) The dragged card stays in its grid cell (no free-floating follow-the-pointer layer); it lifts by a shadow and a static 3 px offset, never a transition (law 12 reduced motion, and no motion that could mislead about position). (3) Into a nest: the hit test uses the committed layout, and while the pointer is over a nest the rest of the grid stops reflowing (otherwise the pin pushes the nest away from the pointer). The whole subgrid lights (dashed intent outline, tint) because a joining member flows at the nest's end, not at a cell; palette drags onto a nest light it the same way and no longer draw a cell rect inside it. Safety ops and nests are never offered to a nest (placeable). (4) Out of a nest: leaving the nest BODY's visible rect (not the inner grid's, which a scrolling nest hides) hands the card to the parent grid, which shows the landing rect; release writes the top-level position first, then nestOut (one undo step). (5) Fixed on the way: Out on the home used nestRemove, so a member placed into a nest from the palette (no top-level entry) vanished from the home; Out now uses nestOut (look and size kept, flows unplaced when it never had a top-level place). (6) Fixed on the way: a keyed #each reordering the dragged node dropped pointer capture and stranded the drag; DOM order is frozen while any drag is in flight, and lostpointercapture ends a drag. title: Factory plugin: Advanced Penetration GUI (RFC-068 substitute for generator-advanced)
design:
Factory plugin "Advanced Penetration": the first plugin shipped in the repo (plugins/factory/advanced-penetration/), installed and enabled by default in the shell, removable (disable) like any plugin, same v1 contract. Substitutes RENDERING 10 generator-advanced per RFC-068 (RENDERING 10.2): registerHero with replaces 'advanced-generator', require = pattern.running + advgen.master + the six base roles (RFC-081, the same essential set as roles.js ADVGEN_SPEC), optional source.background_run, advgen.mode, action.store; modulators (RFC-066 mod.* roles, entry key 20 mod_target) claimed as per-entry instances (min 0) and drawn under the base control each rides. advgen.mode is essential only when pattern.select is present (RENDERING 10): the claim cannot express a conditional, so mount throws and the host falls back (10.2 item 5).

fray-d reference (github.com/fray-d/OSSM-Lite @ d20afa5, read 2026-10-02):
- docs/preset.html (the web config GUI): Master Speed, Max Depth, Min Depth, In Speed, Out Speed, In Acceleration, Out Acceleration, in that order; each base control carries its modifier table in a collapsible <details> directly under its slider (Amplitude, To Min, At Min, To Max, At Max, Offset); presets: Load + list + Delete, name + Save; rename was a three-step load/save/delete (we have the rename op); presets never carry master speed or depths (safety).
- docs/play.html: in/out speed are percentages of master; accel low = smooth, high = robotic; master 0 holds position. Modifier amplitude locks the other modifier fields until set (100 = off on fray-d; RFC-066 flips it to mod.amount 0 = off).
- Software/src/ossm/advanced_penetration/advanced_penetration_structs.h: Modifier::getModification is the cycling trapezoid (in_step ramp, in_wait hold, out_step ramp back, out_wait rest, offset phase in steps), cycle = stroke pairs; depth modulation pulls toward the opposing depth, other controls toward 0.
- advanced_penetration_ui.h drawStroke/calculateStroke: the stroke picture is depth (y) over time (x), the in half and out half each as wide as its stroke time from speed and accel (trapezoid velocity profile, bezier easing ratio accelTime/totalTime), plus a dotted outline of the maximum modulated stroke; drawBars: the modifier preview is a bar per step of the cycle.

Control map: stroke picture (depth window band on the rail, in half and out half from speed/accel); Master; Depth window (depth_max, depth_min); In stroke (speed_in, accel_in); Out stroke (speed_out, accel_out); every modulator as a <details> under its target with amount, rise, hold, fall, rest, phase (+ shape select when present) and a static cycle preview from reported values (no live phase cursor: the hub reports no modulator phase, so a moving cursor would claim machine state nobody reported); run/stop + background_run + mode in the head; presets list via the store (RFC-070 store_id) with save/load/rename/delete through action.store (RFC-067).
acceptance_criteria: Factory plugin loads by default in the shell and can be disabled; substitutes generator-advanced only when every essential binding resolves, else the host renders the generic widget or settings-card; every write through api.write with the law 5 ladder, gray-with-reason, law 12 targets, no red; npm run check zero, npm test green, plugins.test covers factory loading and the substitution fallback; Playwright on the fake hub with the role-carrying fixture; live smoke against valencesim once it carries the roles.

title: RFC-077: survive live catalog growth (subscribe 0x0001, refetch in the background, CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN, placements of withdrawn channels)
description:
RFC-077 (Valence rfc-cou) ACCEPTED, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:32): subscribing to catalog 0x0001 is a MUST for every client; a user-space change keeps readiness, the client refetches in the background and sends CATALOG_READY with the new etag; withdrawn grants get one unsolicited NACK CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN; appeared channels deliver nothing until subscribed; no base etag (degraded mode for pinned clients). Risk accepted: stale layouts are covered by the byte-identical core guarantee and law 10 inert keys.

Change: src/model/machine.svelte.js applies a new catalog etag without a reconnect or a full UI reset (shadow, pending writes and open confirms on unaffected channels survive), subscribes to appeared accessory channels the user has placed, and treats withdrawn channels' placements as missing (ties to ph-uoh's orphan rendering); CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN is shown once per channel, not as a refusal storm. The session-layer half (subscribe, refetch, CATALOG_READY) is Valence clients/js (rfc-58u).

Prove it: fixture-replay test: an etag change adds and removes a user-space channel mid-session with no reconnect and no lost pending write elsewhere; live smoke once Nucleus val-9u0.12 or valencesim grows its catalog.
close_reason: Landed in 45e56ae: second catalog adoption in one session = in-place rebuild (survivors keep samples/grants/shadows/confirms; vanished channels drop samples+grants so placements go inert; appeared channels subscribed via wishes.js regrow); 0x0001 wished at critical priority (never shed) whenever the hub declares it; changed 0x0001 snapshot mid-session -> background session.requestCatalog() while LIVE holds (TODO(rfc-58u)); CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN NACK logged once per channel, grant dropped. Tests: test/wishes.test.mjs fixture replay (one channel appears, one leaves: only the new one wished, only the gone one removed, survivors untouched; 0x0001 never shed). Shadow survival is structural (shadow.svelte.js is never reset on catalog), not node-tested. Live: subscriptions unchanged on valencesim (first-adoption path; grants as before). OWED: live growth smoke -- valencesim declares no 0x0001 and never grows (needs Nucleus val-9u0.12 or a sim growth step), and valence-js rfc-58u (until it lands the refetch adopts with verified=false and is not cached). VETO-ABLE: all appeared h2c channels are subscribed (the generic policy), not only placed ones.

title: RFC-087/059: timed motion sender fills segments bundles to the advertised horizon and leads media by schedule_latency_us
description:
RFC-087 (Valence rfc-66i), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:06, 01:08), and RFC-059 (rfc-r4v) ACCEPTED (comment 00:28; clients SHOULD lead media by schedule_latency_us and MUST NOT hardcode it).

Change:
- Lookahead senders (TCode/funscript plugin input, any timed source) use the segments-kind STREAM and fill each bundle up to the hub-advertised horizon from the GRANT (250 default, 500 or 1000), up to 32 segments / 242 B. The horizon caps start stamps; each segment executes at its stamp. A low-latency sender stamps ~50 ms ahead in small bundles under the same horizon. Samples-kind keeps its 20 ms span.
- Media lead = the grant's schedule_latency_us; no hand-tuned offset anywhere in Phosphor.
- Seek/skip flush: use exactly the spelling the RFC-087 draft lands (pause then resume, or a dedicated flush op/seq rule).
- RFC-058 (rfc-zj1) is ACCEPTED: ph-vdk.35's routing of timed input to the segments STREAM is unblocked and lands with this bead.

Likely files: src/model/motion.js (createMotionDoor, FALLBACK_RATE_HZ), src/plugins/host.js, the TCode adapter path; Valence clients/js sender exposes both grant keys (rfc-cl6).

Prove it: unit test: bundles never exceed the advertised horizon or 32 segments; lead equals the fixture grant's schedule_latency_us; live smoke against valencesim and one bench pass with MultiFunPlayer TCode at horizon 250 and 1000 (ph-vdk.27's loader path).
close_reason: Landed in 08b839a: timed input -> segments STREAM {input.target, input.duration, end_velocity unspecified}, start = hub now + grant.scheduleLatencyUs (no constant), within grant.scheduleHorizonMs; bundleHead packs a timed list to horizon / 32 / min_transport_payload; per-channel grants; flush = RFC-087 item 5 supersede (each bundle replaces the unstarted tail, no separate op). Tests: plugins.test.mjs (e) segments routing, lead == fixture schedule_latency_us, bundles never pass horizon/32/payload at 250/500/1000. Live (valencesim): segments 0x2101 granted 50 Hz horizon 250 lead 1000 us; 11 timed inputs accepted, sync_bundles +11, sync_dropped 0. OWED: MultiFunPlayer TCode bench pass at horizon 250 and 1000 in the shell (sim grants only 250); a lookahead source (funscript) has no plugin API yet, bundleHead is ready for it. VETO-ABLE: lead is schedule_latency_us only, not RFC-087's illustrative 50 ms client lead; if real links show deadline_stretched anomalies, add the measured CLOCK rtt/2, still no hand-tuned constant.

title: RFC-062: document the renderer-class boundaries and enforce the derived floor as the desktop minimum window
description:
RFC-062 (Valence rfc-l8p) ACCEPTED, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:01), open question 1: RENDERING 12.1 RECOMMENDS boundary values informatively in CSS px (handheld/full near 600 to 960, the client's choice stated) and defines the FLOOR by derivation: the width at which the persistent strip still holds its mandatory controls at law 12's 40 px targets. Below the floor no client degrades further; a desktop client MUST enforce the floor as its OS minimum window size (Phosphor: 320 today).

Change: state Phosphor's chosen boundaries (src/model/rclass.js GLANCE_DOWN 216 etc. and the handheld/full split) in docs/DESIGN.md with the RENDERING 12.1 pointer; derive the floor from the strip's mandatory controls (e-stop + pause after RFC-085, at 40 px) and set src-tauri/tauri.conf.json windows[0].minWidth to it (320 today; ph-vdk.40 tracks dropping it once sub-320 layout holds, so the two must agree with the derivation). The class switch keeps content, category, pending writes and open confirms (already the RFC's rule).

Prove it: test/renderer-class.test.mjs asserts the documented constants; test/shell-chrome-geometry.test.mjs asserts minWidth equals the derived floor; npm run check zero findings.

title: RFC-083: color and datetime archetypes by role (RGB; datetime in hub time converted with the CLOCK offset)
description:
RFC-083 (Valence rfc-vdc) ACCEPTED option B, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:19): the archetype hint is struck; row 4 pad2d binds by identity, rows 16/17 (color, datetime) by role.

Change:
- color: bind color.red/green/blue (RGB only; no HSV role set exists, a hub converts in firmware). A picker writes the three fields as one intent.
- datetime: datetime.moment / datetime.start / datetime.end carry HUB TIME (seconds in the hub's section 7.1 timebase), never Unix epoch. Phosphor converts to wall time with the CLOCK offset it already holds, and back on write. A stored moment is valid for the hub's current boot_id: on a boot_id change the client marks it stale and re-arms (never silently shifts it).
- Remove any archetype-hint read from the settings model.

Likely files: src/model/settings.js (archetype projection), src/model/roles.js, src/ui/Field.svelte or new widgets, src/model/machine.svelte.js (CLOCK offset, boot_id).

Prove it: settings-model test: fixture fields with the roles project to color/datetime; datetime round trip through a fixed CLOCK offset is exact; a boot_id change marks the value stale; no hub emits these today, so fixtures only (state it on close).
close_reason: Landed in 549665b: archetype hint read removed; color.red/green/blue per group -> one color picker (writes coalesce into one intent on a shared write channel); datetime.* -> row 17 datetime-local over hub seconds via format.js hubSecToWallMs/wallMsToHubSec (CLOCK hub-us + telemetry.uptime wrap), disabled with a reason when no uptime; machine.link.bootId from WELCOME; a moment this page armed reads stale after a boot_id change and offers Re-arm (never shifted). Tests: settings-model.test.mjs (projection, partial/read-only triples decline, hint ignored, exact round trip through a fixed CLOCK ref, boot_id stale). FIXTURES ONLY: no hub emits color/datetime roles today (valencesim d49f36ed905e65bb has none); page smoke on the sim shows no regressions. VETO-ABLE: an interval (datetime.start+end) is two inputs in one group, not a dedicated range picker; staleness tracks only moments this page armed (in memory).

title: RFC-066/081: advanced-generator widget binds advgen.* masters and groups modulators under their mod_target
description:
RFC-066 ACCEPTED AS AMENDED (Valence rfc-0sm) and RFC-081 ACCEPTED (rfc-bf4), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 00:07). Changes the generator-advanced widget landed in 10db388 (ph-vdk.11).

Change:
- Masters bind by the registered advgen.* roles (roles.js TODO(rfc-bf4)).
- 'Lane' is retired: draft lane.* roles (roles.js ~124-129, ~334-342) become the mod.* family: mod.amount, mod.rise, mod.hold, mod.fall, mod.rest, mod.phase, optional mod.shape (absent = cycling trapezoid). Field units carry the clock (strokes or seconds).
- A modulator is one entry; its entry-level mod_target (channel id, field index) names the field it rides. A complete modulator RENDERS AS A GROUP ATTACHED UNDER ITS TARGET wherever that field is placed (inside the widget, and under the field if the user placed it elsewhere in the builder). generator-advanced = advgen base controls plus whatever modulators target them; the 'four or more' minimum is withdrawn (decline rules in the widget update accordingly).
- mod.amount 0 = no modulation (Nucleus flips its 100 = off in the same release, val-091.38); default display and any 'off' affordance follow.

Likely files: src/model/roles.js, src/ui/hero/AdvancedGeneratorWidget.svelte, src/ui/heroes.js, test/advanced-generator.test.mjs, test/lane-palette.test.mjs (rename). Needs clients/js to decode mod_target (Valence rfc-9u2).

Prove it: test/advanced-generator.test.mjs rewritten: modulators group under their targets, a modulator whose target is absent is drawn nowhere (or as missing per law), masters decline when an advgen role is missing; live smoke against valencesim with the reference catalog.
