title: DashGrid: nests read untracked while the view map is missing; announce region anchored to the viewport
description: Two grid-layer bugs found building the home (ph-e82.5). (1) dashboard.svelte.js read() is G.viewMap(..., false): when the view's map does not exist yet, grid.js own() checks a missing key on the layout proxy, which Svelte does not track, and returns a fresh plain {}. DashGrid's nests derived then never re-runs when the map is created, so New nest on a view the user never arranged stores the nest but draws nothing until remount. Root fix: read() also reads Object.keys(layouts.layouts[layouts.active]) (or viewMap tracks). Home.svelte works around it by creating its map in an effect.pre; category pages are still affected. (2) DashGrid's .sr-only announce div is position:absolute with no positioned ancestor, so its containing block is the initial containing block; as an abspos child of the flex .dash-wrap its static position is the grid's top. When anything above the grid pushes that below the fold (the home palette; HubPicker in a short window) the document grows, and scrolling it carries the top strip off screen (law 11; responsive-matrix stripCheck caught it at 1280x720). Root fix: .dash-wrap { position: relative }. Home.svelte contains it via .home { position: relative }.
close_reason: Fixed in 8a6d51f: grid.js own() reads the value first (subscribes to a missing key on a proxy); .dash-wrap position: relative; Home workarounds removed. Evidence: nest.test (New nest on a never-arranged view draws, failed before), responsive-matrix --only home (announce region contained, strip checks pass), grid-model, home.test.

title: buttplug fork: StopCmd ignores its device index; device index allocation races
description:
Found building ph-e82.8 part 2 (toys as modules). Both in ../ButtplugIO (branch valence), not Phosphor code.

1. ServerDeviceManager::stop_devices (crates/buttplug_server/src/device/server_device_manager.rs) stops EVERY device and ignores StopCmdV4's device_index/feature_index. StopDeviceCmd v0..v3 converts to StopCmd(Some(index)), so an Intiface app stopping one toy stops all of them. Phosphor's bp_toy_stop works around it by sending zero outputs (docs/BUTTPLUG.md, Toy stops).

2. DeviceConfigurationManager::device_index (crates/buttplug_server_device_config/src/device_config_manager.rs) computes a free index from user_device_definitions and inserts later, with no lock across connect tasks; two devices finishing their connection together get the same index and the second replaces the first in the device map (reproduced with three upstream simulated devices in one scan: one of the three never lists). Phosphor's cargo tests run one simulated toy per server for this reason.

Fix home is the fork (upstream PR candidate). Acceptance: a StopDeviceCmd for one device leaves another device's output untouched; N simulated devices found in one scan all list with distinct indices.
close_reason: Fixed in the fork, branch valence: 36110484 (StopCmd with a device index stops only that device; unknown index is DeviceNotAvailable; no index still stops all) and b898a4d1 (device index allocated atomically with its insert). Phosphor 185bc64: bp_toy_stop is StopCmd(Some(index), outputs only) and the cargo toy tests run three simulated toys plus the machine in one scan, 13/13 passed on ten runs.

Tests in buttplug_tests/tests/test_simulated_devices.rs: test_simulated_stop_one_device_leaves_other_running (failed before, passes) and test_simulated_devices_found_together_get_distinct_indices (3 simulated devices in one scan on a 4-worker multi-thread runtime, 10 rounds per run; failed 3/3 before, 10/10 runs pass after). Phosphor workarounds: both can be removed. src-tauri path-depends on the fork working tree, so the fixes are already live. bp_toy_stop / Buttplug::toy_stop can send StopCmdV4::new(Some(index), None, false, true) (outputs only, write-acknowledged, uses the device's own stop set) instead of per-feature zero OutputCmds; pass inputs=true only if a toy stop should also drop sensor subscriptions. title: A stale intent's late rejection clobbers a newer write on the same shadow record
description:
shadow.svelte.js flush(): when an INTENT gets no answer, the shadow's own FAULT_MS (2 s) timer faults the record first ('no echo'); the session's sendIntent timeout (3 s, session.js) then rejects the same promise and flush's catch calls fail() on whatever the record holds NOW. If the operator wrote again in that 1 s window, the newer write is marked fault ('refused: Error'), its requested value discarded, and lastRefusal updated, although that newer write is still in flight and may yet confirm. Transient ground-truth defect (law 4/5): the control states a refusal the hub never made. Seen in test/control-contract.test.mjs (it now sleeps 1.2 s after its silent-hub step to keep runs independent).

Fix sketch: tag each shadow record with the send it belongs to (sentAt or an intent counter captured in flush) and ignore a settle/fail from an older send.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN: control-contract silent step without the drain sleep: write, wait for fault, write again within 1 s, assert the second write is pending (not fault) until its own echo.
acceptance_criteria: A late rejection never changes a record that a newer write owns; control-contract passes without the drain sleep.
close_reason: Acceptance met: test/control-contract.test.mjs drops the drain sleep and checks a newer write survives the silent intent's late timeout (fails x3 on pre-8f66ce0 shadow, passes on HEAD). Fix 8f66ce0, test 5c03422.

title: Builder (g): embed buttplug in the shell as an Intiface-compatible server; machine via the intent path, toys as modules
description:
Phase (g), DESIGN §10.8. Embed a buttplug server in the Tauri shell (Rust crates from ../buttplug: buttplug_server, buttplug_server_device_config, the btleplug/serial/hid hardware managers, a websocket server connector) speaking the Intiface-compatible server protocol, so games and apps built for Intiface Central connect to Phosphor. The machine is a buttplug device whose commands enter the kernel intent path (host.js submitMotion, the TCode adapter's door, motion permission), never a second Valence session; the fork's buttplug_server_hwmgr_slopsync (own WS session, mDNS) is NOT linked. Toys found by the hardware managers appear as modules (phase c contract) and as relationship targets (see the relationship CANON FLAG in DESIGN §10.8). Listener binds loopback by default; LAN exposure waits on ph-vdk.28. Desktop first; Android is its own later question.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- cargo test in src-tauri for the device-to-intent bridge: a LinearCmd maps to one submitMotion call with the same 0..1 position and duration as the TCode adapter's mapping for the same input.
- Loopback client test (buttplug's client crate, or a JSON fixture over ws://127.0.0.1): handshake, RequestDeviceList returns the machine, a LinearCmd reaches the fake kernel.
- Against valencesim: a buttplug client drives the machine; a second raw Valence session sees the motion, and the hub reports exactly one session from Phosphor.
- By hand: a real Intiface-targeting app connects with no change beyond the port; a BLE toy appears as a module; the strip e-stop halts the machine while the buttplug client keeps sending.
acceptance_criteria: An Intiface-targeting app drives the machine through Phosphor on loopback with one Valence session; toys appear as modules; the strip e-stop wins over a live buttplug stream; the listed tests pass.

Fork (branch valence): 0def2f04 ServerDeviceManager::disconnect_device, 1d4c51ee valence machine Vibrate output (writes nothing; device config 5.32), 35c8344f websocket server on_client_accepted (peer address).

New commands: bp_settings, bp_settings_set(settings), bp_device_rename(key, name), bp_device_disconnect(index), bp_device_forget(key), bp_clients, bp_client_disconnect(id); bp_scan_start takes optional seconds. New event bp://clients; bp://log gains time; bp_devices gains protocol, address, device_name, display_name and lists remembered (connected:false) devices. All in docs/BUTTPLUG.md. ServerPane stays self-contained (no props, exports nothing new); tabs live in src/shell/server/*.

VETO-ABLE DECISIONS (each reversible on a word):
1. Settings persist Rust-side as settings.json in the app config dir (buttplug/), not localStorage: start-on-launch then runs from Rust setup whether or not any pane is mounted (the drawer may mount it lazily), and the device config already lives Rust-side.
2. The port and the hardware managers are refused while the server runs (Intiface Central locks them too), so saved settings always describe the running server. Log level and start-on-launch apply at once.
3. "Allow raw messages" NOT offered (pushback): the fork speaks spec v4 and implements no raw read/write commands in any spec version, so the setting would drive nothing (webui.md: a control that drives nothing is a defect). The settings tab says so in one line.
4. Upstream buttplug log lines reach bp://log only where Phosphor owns the process logger (release builds); in debug builds tauri-plugin-log owns it and they go to the dev console. Moving that would mean editing lib.rs setup beyond registration lines.
5. The device config is upstream's user device config file (devices.json, save_user_config/load_protocol_configs), saved on every device-list change and every rename/forget, write-then-rename under one lock. Rename applies to bp_devices at once; connected apps see it from the toy's next connection (upstream copies the name at connect).
6. The machine refuses rename, disconnect and forget: its identity is documented as fixed and it comes and goes with the hub link.
7. Forget is refused while connected; remembered devices (connected:false) are listed after connected ones so they can be forgotten.
8. The pane's scan is timed at 30 s (SCAN_S) and stops itself unless another scan request comes first; Rust takes any seconds or none.
9. Scan state now flips where the scan is requested (Buttplug::scan), not in the machine manager, so it shows with the machine manager off.
10. Clients: one at a time as before (Intiface parity); message rate is counted per whole second server-side; connected-since is the server host's clock. bp://clients emits at most 1 Hz while name or rate changes.
11. Log: 500 lines kept, level filter is view-only, copy is plain text with ISO times; the latest error line shows under the status row until the next start request.
12. Hit targets are 40 px for every pane control (law 12), up from 36 px on fine pointers.
13. tokio "time" is named in src-tauri/Cargo.toml (outside the listed ownership; one word) for the scan timer and the client rate tick.
14. Machine Vibrate: Vibrate only, 0..100 steps; Rotate not added (no consumer asked). bp_toy_* still refuse the machine.

TESTS: cargo test 13/13 (new: settings_persist_and_gate_the_managers, device_config_rename_disconnect_forget, timed_scan_stops_itself, clients_list_rate_and_operator_disconnect; loopback and stop-all extended for the machine Vibrate); fork cargo test -p buttplug_server valence 2/2, -p buttplug_transport_websocket_tungstenite 2/2; npm run check and npm test green; test/server-pane.test.mjs covers every new command path with a fake invoke/listen.

OWED (by hand, Tauri window): a real Intiface-targeting app connects, shows in clients with its name, its rate moves, disconnect closes it; a real BLE toy appears in devices with its battery read, rename shows, disconnect then forget work, and the timed scan ends; start-on-launch starts the server on a fresh launch; settings.json and devices.json land in the app config dir; a vibrate-only app's vibrate reaches the node graph. No live check of the UI geometry inside the sibling's drawer.

title: Builder (e): nests (scrolling or fixed subgrids) and saveable nests
description:
Phase (e), DESIGN §10.6. A nest is a control holding a subgrid, scrolling or fixed by the user's choice. A nest with its contents is saveable as a reusable module, stored with the layouts, keyed on roles or uids (law 10). Placing a saved nest on a machine that lacks some bindings leaves those members inert, never an error. A scrolling nest must not hide pending or degraded state (RENDERING §9 invariant): its frame shows the in-flight count, as drillCard does in App.svelte today. The placement rule for single fields (anywhere vs nests-only) comes from the rulings bead.

TEST/VALIDATION PLAN:
- test/grid-model.test.mjs: nest serialize/deserialize round trip; a saved nest reinserted under a different catalog keeps inert members and survives another round trip.
- Playwright on the fake-hub harness: a pending write inside a scrolled-away region of a scrolling nest shows on the nest frame; the count clears on echo.
- test/responsive-matrix.mjs: a nested scroll never traps page scroll on phone viewports.
acceptance_criteria: Nests hold subgrids, save as reusable modules, reinsert on another catalog with inert members; a pending write inside a nest is visible on its frame.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-01 landed (see commit). Decisions recorded as VETO-ABLE:
1. ph-e82.1 item 4 (single fields anywhere vs nests-only) stays OPEN. Coded both ways behind FIELDS_NESTS_ONLY in src/model/grid.js (default false = anywhere); placeable(kind, inNest, nestsOnly) is the one rule the palette and DashGrid read. Flip the constant to rule nests-only.
2. Storage: a nest is an entry in its view's placement map, id nest:<n> (client-made, never wire vocabulary, law 10), carrying {title, scroll, map}; the member map's keys ARE the membership, null = not yet placed. Members the catalog lacks stay inert: never drawn, never deleted, counted in edit mode only ("N not on this machine").
3. Modules (saved nests) live in the same phosphor.layouts store under `modules`, shared by every layout, class and view, keyed on the members' stable ids. A taken module name is refused, never silently overwritten.
4. An item that is a member of any nest is drawn inside it, never also at the top level; one control may sit in two nests (a module inserted twice). Nests never nest.
5. The frame count mirrors drillCard: every member field not confirmed (pending, overdue, fault) counts, on every nest (not only scrolling ones), in a bar outside the scroll region that is always drawn so the count never shifts layout (law 5).
6. Stacked (<= 640 CSS px) a nest never scrolls by itself, so it cannot trap the page scroll; ph-e82.7 may revisit.
7. Reset layout forgets positions only: nests keep size and members and reflow. Ungroup returns present members to the top level and discards the nest's inert members with it.
8. Nests render on every DashGrid view, including the derived category pages (arrangement only; every field stays reachable). If the home should be the only nest surface, gate it in App, not grid.js.
Root-cause fix found on the way: a key deleted from a Svelte $state proxy still answers hasOwnProperty (svelte 5.56 deleteProperty never deletes from the target), so grid.js own() lied after any delete: a member moved out could not be added back, and switchLayout to a deleted layout name would succeed and then crash viewMap. own() now also requires a defined value; grid-model covers it.
Tests: grid-model (nest round trip, reinsertion under a different catalog keeping inert members, second round trip, flag both ways, the proxy ghost); test/nest.test.mjs (check:nest, in test:browser) on the fake hub: a held write on a scrolled-away member shows "1 in flight" on the frame outside the scroll region, clears on echo, plus the edit flow (ungroup, new, add, save module, out, re-add, insert); responsive-matrix `nest` scenario at 320/360/390: no nested scroll region, a wheel over the nest scrolls the page, phone checks pass.

All acceptance criteria met; close once ph-e82.5 lands or the dependency is dropped.

title: Draft the Phosphor-discovered spec gaps into Valence RFC-QUEUE
description:
MISSING: Phosphor hits several places where Valence is silent or self-contradictory. Per doctrine, code does not bind to an unaccepted clause; these need RFC drafts in Valence spec/RFC-QUEUE.md (the one writable door), then rulings, then the Phosphor beads that depend on them.

THE LIST (details in the epic report):
1. Live renderer-class selection for a resizable viewport (RENDERING §12 silent beyond "adopts the nearer one").
2. The `destructive` flag referenced by RENDERING §8.2 row 6 / §8.4 / registry ui_archetypes has no wire carrier (SPEC §8.8 setting_flags has no such bit).
3. RENDERING §8.4 `select` says index 0 is filler for every select; SPEC §8.9 (line 738) limits that to action.* op tables. Contradiction.
4. Identifying a device-authored anomaly/event channel and labeling its event kinds (SPEC line 1388 deferred it; Phosphor currently regexes names).
5. Advanced-generator lane count: RENDERING §2.2 says four lanes; Nucleus emits six. Make the lane count catalog-declared.
6. `action.preset` (Nucleus) is not a registered action tag (registry has preset_save/preset_recall).
7. Tier-2 substituted-widget conformance (RENDERING §10/§13 silent) - co-own with the plugin-surface agent.
8. Client-pushed provisioning of a fresh hub (RFC-054 frames only hub-disclosure).

ACCEPTANCE: each item is either an RFC-QUEUE draft or a recorded decision that no RFC is needed; the Phosphor beads that depend on one link to it.
notes: Drafted 2026-09-25 in Valence spec/RFC-QUEUE.md (commits 9f6ee9d..0199b2d), one rfc- bead each on the Valence board: (1) renderer-class selection RFC-062 rfc-l8p [ph-vdk.5]; (2) destructive flag carrier RFC-063 rfc-c5u [ph-vdk.4, ph-vdk.3]; (3) index-0 filler scope RFC-064 rfc-8pk [ph-vdk.3]; (4) event purpose roles + kind labels RFC-065 rfc-x3n [ph-vdk.7, ph-vdk.14]; (5) advanced-generator lanes RFC-066 rfc-0sm [ph-vdk.11]; (6) action.preset -> registered action.store op select RFC-067 rfc-2n5 [ph-vdk.11, ph-vdk.3]; (7) substituted-widget conformance RFC-068 rfc-8qh (cross-refs RFC-061, the TCode-adapter plugin entry another agent drafted the same day, still uncommitted at close); (8) client-pushed WiFi provisioning RFC-069 rfc-qf5 [ph-vdk.24]. All DRAFT, rulings pending. Dependent Phosphor beads should not bind to these clauses until accepted.
close_reason: Eight RFC drafts landed in Valence RFC-QUEUE (RFC-062..069), beads rfc-l8p/c5u/8pk/x3n/0sm/2n5/8qh/qf5

title: Keyboard and accessibility basics: tablist roving, user text size, reactive reduced motion
description:
MISSING: both nav tablists (rail and phone strip) and the LogPane tabs lack arrow-key roving focus and aria-controls/tabpanel wiring. The root font-size is a pixel value, so the operator's browser/OS text-size preference has no effect (it also means a 4K display at 100% scaling gets 18px text in a 1680px column). Several labels sit at .56-.62rem (~10px). Two components read prefers-reduced-motion once at module load and ignore later changes.

EVIDENCE: App.svelte:321-335 and :349-354, LogPane.svelte:118-124, style.css:164 (`font-size: calc(var(--s) * 16px)`), style.css:506 (.app max-width 1680px), SafetyBar.svelte chip labels (.56-.62rem), LinkBar.svelte chip (.62rem), RailWidget.svelte:332-333, LinkBar.svelte:148-149. RENDERING.md §13 law 12 (reduced motion is a floor), §8.3 full class ("keyboard-typeable").

ACCEPTANCE: WAI-ARIA tabs pattern on every tablist; root size scales with the user default (percent/rem based) with --s still applying; no text under ~11px at default scale; reduced-motion changes take effect live. Any global keyboard shortcut for stop is an operator ruling first (see epic judgment calls).
notes: Closed 2026-09-25, commit d5846aa. Roving tabindex + Arrow-key nav on both tablists (rail vertical, phone strip horizontal), Tab leaves in one step. rail-collapse gets aria-label. html font-size moved from calc(--s*16px) to calc(--s*100%) (style.css) so the browser's own text-size default is honored, --s still multiplies on top -- verified 22.40px at a 20px default via CDP Page.setFontSizes, no overflow at 360/1280w. Added a :focus-visible ring on the range slider thumb (style.css), the one control whose outline:none had no visible replacement. RailWidget.svelte and LinkBar.svelte's prefers-reduced-motion reads were one-time snapshots (rAF loop / heatmap tick) -- converted to matchMedia().addEventListener('change', ...), same live pattern as PlanStrip/TelemetryChart; verified live toggle with no reload. LogPane's aria-live=polite and ConfirmLayer's focus trap/return were already correct on inspection, no changes needed. Dropped role=tabpanel/aria-controls wiring: <main> is a landmark per this codebase's own rule and Svelte's a11y linter correctly rejected an interactive role on it; roving focus is the literal scope asked for. No global e-stop keyboard shortcut added (operator ruling required). Tests: test/a11y-basics.test.mjs (24 checks, all pass), wired into npm run test:browser. responsive-matrix stays at 0 findings; shell-chrome-geometry unaffected.

title: Shell BLE: no automatic BLE-to-WS upgrade, scan-response flags unread, MTU never requested
description:
MISSING: SPEC §13.1 says clients SHOULD auto-upgrade BLE to WS; the shell only offers a manual button. The scan response's ble_adv_flags (pairing_window_open, ws_available) are never read, so the hub list cannot show either. MTU is read but not negotiated (SPEC §13.4 asks for >= 250 before catalog transfer). A relaunch re-joins only WS hubs; a BLE-only operator starts from scratch.

EVIDENCE: ShellBar.svelte canUpgrade/upgrade (manual), ble-ws.js:66 (getMtu only), main.js:70-73 (ws-only auto-connect), SPEC.md §13.1 line ~1172, §13.4 lines ~1192-1194, §6.3 (ws_port 46 / ipv4 47, 0 means absent), RFC-046 (same instance_id re-HELLO is a migration).

ACCEPTANCE: after a live BLE session whose WELCOME carries ws_port and ipv4, the shell migrates to WS with the same instance_id and falls back to BLE if WS fails; scan rows show pairing-window and WS-available badges; MTU is requested before catalog transfer where the platform allows. Depends on the UUID bug.

[verified 2026-09-25 -- node test/ble-adv.test.mjs pass; set_android_mtu allowed by ACL in the release build]. NOT verified on a radio: Nucleus has no BLE yet. Left open for the live BLE-session acceptance. Not done: relaunch re-join of a BLE-only hub. MSD company id unpinned: RFC-072 (rfc-uvh).

title: Tier-1 safety bar + anomaly log: anomalies hidden in a Console tab, safety edges unrendered
description:
MISSING: the founding Tier-1 pair (DESIGN.md §3) is half done. Anomalies are only visible under Console > Log > Anomalies; nothing in the persistent or utility region says one arrived. safety-events (0x000E) edges, the EVENT twin of the safety latch, are not shown as safety history at all (they land in the session ring). Device-authored event kinds have no labels, so an anomaly renders as raw numbers.

EVIDENCE: LogPane.svelte:23-28 and :120-121, machine.svelte.js:422-429, registry.yaml core_channels 0x000E, SPEC.md line 1388 (event_kind labels deliberately deferred), Nucleus motion-anomaly EVENT (ValenceCatalog.h:1101).

ACCEPTANCE: an unread-anomaly count/indicator in the safety strip or link strip that clears on view; a safety history built from 0x000E reconciled against the 0x0003 latch via seq_of_state; event bodies render generically (key=value, never dropped, §10 event-stream). Channel identification per the name-matching bead.
notes:
02a9aab: dock shows the latest core safety-events (0x000E) edge: kind, age, unread count cleared by viewing LogPane's Safety feed, dimmed+worded stale when the link has not been live since the edge; the Safety feed is the history (bodies render key=value). Bound by CORE_CHANNEL identity. [verified 2026-09-25 -- node test/safety-reach.test.mjs exit 0; responsive matrix 0 findings with the edge line on screen; live valencesim estop_latched/estop_cleared]. STILL OPEN: reconciliation of the 0x000E history against the 0x0003 latch via seq_of_state; device anomaly EVENT channel indicator (blocked on RFC-065 / rfc-x3n, TODO(rfc-x3n) in SafetyBar.svelte and machine.svelte.js).
seq_of_state half landed (machine.svelte.js, LogPane.svelte, SafetyBar.svelte): a
safety-events edge older than the highest seqOfState any accepted edge has
carried is marked superseded (dimmed + a 'superseded' chip in the Safety
feed); the dock's one-line summary skips superseded/diagnostic records and
shows the latest real edge. Reconciliation deliberately never reads the
0x0003 latch's own packed fields (e.g. its per-INITIATION sequence) by name --
that field is THIS device's catalog schema, would trip
check-device-knowledge.mjs, and violates law 6. seqOfState (registry global
key 34) riding the EVENT is the one comparable number available, so "the
current STATE seq" is tracked purely from accepted edges' own seqOfState.
Separately, a latch STATE change with no matching edge (compared OPAQUELY,
never by field) surfaces as a 'latch changed, no event received' diagnostic
line in the feed after a 250ms grace window for wire-order jitter (ponytail:
a fixed timer, not a real join -- noted in-source). Tests added to
test/safety-reach.test.mjs (out-of-order seq_of_state -> superseded; a bare
latch STATE change -> the diagnostic line). Verified: node
test/safety-reach.test.mjs and node test/check-device-knowledge.mjs both
green.
STILL BLOCKED (RFC-065 / rfc-x3n, unchanged from before tonight): the device
anomaly EVENT channel indicator has no catalog key to bind to yet.
2026-10-01 finish: (1) the strip summary now skips superseded edges too (72203c4's TopStrip port carried only the diagnostic skip, so an out-of-order older edge became the headline); (2) the superseded test is SPEC 7.3 serial arithmetic on the u16 seq, not '<' (a plain compare marked every post-wrap edge superseded forever). Reconciliation against the latch STATE frame's own header seq is not reachable: Valence/clients/js/session.js emits 'state' without header.seq, so the newest seq_of_state any accepted edge carried stands in for it. [verified 2026-10-01 -- node test/safety-reach.test.mjs ALL PASS incl. new strip-summary and wrap asserts; live valencesim (machine --homed): strip e-stop then estop clear gave wire edges seqOfState 2,3, strip headline estop latched -> estop cleared, feed 2 rows none superseded, no diagnostic line]
close_reason: Acceptance met except the device anomaly EVENT indicator, which stays blocked on RFC-065 (rfc-x3n) and moves to ph-vdk.39. Safety history from 0x000E reconciled via seq_of_state (serial arithmetic, superseded edges dimmed and kept out of the strip headline), unread count clears on view, bodies render key=value.

title: Value axes and units: no peak companion, scope never shown, unit_ids ignored (RENDERING §5, §6)
description:
MISSING: §5.4 requires scope (session/lifetime/window) to be displayed or unambiguously implied (MUST) and live/peak never confused; companions sharing a role/unit SHOULD render as one instrument. Nucleus sends aspect/scope on the odometer (ValenceCatalog.h:778-803, including peak_mm_s at :788-791) and 33 numeric unit_ids. Phosphor never reads scope, never composes a peak marker (isPeakRole keys on a name suffix and has no caller), and formats units from the free string only.

EVIDENCE: grep finds no scope use in src/; roles.js:187-189 (dead, name-based), format.js:106-110 (free-string unit), Valence clients/js/catalog.js:405-408 (unit_id decoded), RENDERING.md §5.4, §6 formatting and unknown-unit rule.

ACCEPTANCE: totals show their scope; a peak-aspect field renders as a marker on its live companion; reset linkage (§5.4) co-locates the reset with its group behind the confirm layer; unit_id drives suffix and precision with the catalog string as the unknown-id fallback. Fixture-model tests.
close_reason: Done in 76f433e, re-landed as f31bdee after 72c1735 reverted it from a stale shared index [verified 2026-09-25 -- committed tree extracted: device-knowledge PASS, registry-pins PASS, settings-model ALL PASS (peak rides live twin + leaves group; 'Run count · lifetime total'; statTag 'session peak'; unit_id suffix; catalog-string fallback; count whole; hero never binds a peak), valence-wire + telebuf-sim ALL PASS, vite build ok; valencesim fixture decodes aspect/scope/unit_id onto fields]. format.js UNIT_SUFFIX (§6) + statTag + labelFor suffix; settings.js carries scope/unitId, pairs peak->live companion; Field.svelte peak tag + bar marker; roles.js take() skips non-live aspects; dead isPeakRole deleted. NOT DONE: §5.4 reset linkage -- no catalog key lets an intent declare itself a group's reset (meta.reset_gen is STATE-side only), so nothing to bind; needs a spec answer. On Nucleus peak_mm_s has no live mm/s twin in its group, so it renders standalone as 'Peak mm s · session peak'. Not live-device verified.

title: First-run, hub choice and reconnect UX outside the shell (hosted page, file://, failed link)
description:
MISSING: outside Tauri the hub is location.hostname or the dev-only ?hub= parameter; there is no way for an operator to enter or pick a hub. That breaks the ruled HOSTED delivery (DESIGN.md §8: one community URL for hubs that do not serve a UI, and Nucleus serves none today) and file:// opens, which connect to an empty host. The "failed" link phase shows text with no retry action. Watch tier (cross-origin /uitoken) is never explained to the operator, nor is the path to control (pairing).

EVIDENCE: main.js:52-53 and :76, App.svelte:290-306 (boot messages, no action), LinkBar.svelte:37-38 (phases), machine.svelte.js:454 (failed when not retrying). SPEC §13.1 line ~1171 and RFC-043 (a client must not assume the hub served its UI). Nucleus serves only /uitoken, /ota, /diag on :80.

ACCEPTANCE: when no hub is implied by the origin, the page shows a hub entry with remembered hubs (browser storage, per-viewer convenience only); failed shows a Retry; a watch-tier session shows why and links to Pairing; the first catalog adoption shows progress; empty categories and a catalog with zero heroes read as intentional, not broken.
close_reason: Landed in 9a2169a [verified 2026-09-25 -- responsive-matrix --only picker: file:// at 360/1280 renders the picker, refused hub shows retry countdown and Retry now opens a session, dropped link is announced and the reconnect adopts the rebooted hub identity; 0 findings]. Adoption progress and empty-state copy split to a follow-up.

title: generator-advanced (fray-d) pattern is absent; requires the list/roster archetype for the preset store
description:
MISSING: RENDERING §10 marks generator-advanced as a REQUIRED pattern on handheld/full. Phosphor has no component for it, and no `list` archetype (§8.2 row 5: STORE channel + roster STATE) either, so the preset store is unrenderable. Nucleus emits the full shape: pattern-advanced (ValenceCatalog.h:1474), a lane-channel factory (:1583-1653, SIX lanes against the spec's four), a preset STORE kind pattern.frayd (:1675) and its roster (:1700), plus pattern-advanced-cmd and pattern-presets-cmd intents (:2001, :2054). Today those fields land as generic cards (Nucleus flags 44 advanced modifier settings, per App.svelte:132-134).

EVIDENCE: settings.js:117-121 (list archetype "claimed by hero widgets", none exists), heroes.js:39-92 (no advanced generator), RENDERING.md §2.2 advanced-generator row, §8.4 list row (pending is a THIRD state; locked-by-role distinct from empty), §10 roster and generator-advanced rows.

ACCEPTANCE: a roster/list widget (BLOB read of STORE items, pending as a distinct state) usable by any STORE+roster pair (the trust ledger too); a generator-advanced widget with master controls, one lane group per declared lane (count from the catalog, not a constant), preset save/recall, and the background_run toggle beside the master run/stop. Declines when any essential binding is missing. Lane-count mismatch goes to the RFC list.
notes: Four blockers, tracked (2026-09-25): (1) lanes -- RENDERING 2.2/10 says four modifier lanes, Nucleus emits six with a different field set and no lane field roles -- RFC-066 / rfc-0sm. (2) store verbs -- Nucleus tags preset CRUD action.preset (unregistered), registry has preset_save/preset_recall with zero emitters and no delete/rename tags -- RFC-067 / rfc-2n5. (3) roster-to-store link -- SPEC 8.7 defines a STORE + roster STATE pair with no key tying them, so a renderer can only guess by name (law 6 forbids it) -- RFC-070 / rfc-ind. (4) JS store-blob fetch -- clients/js/session.js handleBlobChunk drops every blob chunk with ns != 0 and exposes no store BLOB_REQ API, so STORE items are unreadable from any JS client regardless of the spec/registry rulings above -- Valence bead rfc-0d9. This bead proceeds once (3) and (4) land (read path) and (1)/(2) are ruled on (bind path).
close_reason: Delivered by ph-vdk.44/.45; verified live 2026-10-03 on valencesim 0.1.6-p4hub (1280x800): the advanced generator widget draws running + background_run in its head, 9 base controls with 8 modulators each grouped under its target (none loose), the preset ActionField and a 24-slot roster; save/load/delete round trip proven on the wire by actions-live (6d800af), no page errors

title: Display latency: telemetry->numeral is +140 ms (measured); cut it (higher grant rate, smaller LEAD_MS/render delay) and measure the Tauri shell separately
description: Measured 2026-09-21 against Nucleus 88fd666 in Chromium (Vite dev): hub +20 ms, Phosphor +140 ms, end to end +160 ms, corr 0.98, amplitude preserved. telebuf.js LEAD_MS 30 / MAX_LEAD_MS 150 and createRenderClock delay clamp(20..120, p95_gap*1.5+frameDt) were sized for the S3's clumpy 25 Hz arrivals; the P4 delivers every 35 ms with p95 40 ms, so the same arithmetic gives ~29 ms at a 60 Hz grant (machine.svelte.js TELEMETRY_HZ=25 is a measured choice for the S3, re-measure). Also measure inside phosphor.exe (WebView2), which the operator uses; the instrument is Nucleus/tools/lag_probe.py --dump plus a rAF sampler of .hn-val.mono. Never trade truth for smoothness: T18 (arrival stamping) still binds.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Code side (sha in next comment): the dominant client term was not LEAD_MS or the render delay but a RATCHET in telebuf push(): ts = max(arrival+lead, prev+EMA period) only ever moves forward, so EMA noise walks the schedule up to MAX_LEAD_MS (150) and it stays there; the cap then stores arrival+150, i.e. arrival stamping with an offset (T18). Sim (test/telebuf-sim.mjs, P4-like 35-45 ms arrivals): display lag p95 187 ms before, 93 ms after. Changes: respace at 0.98 x EMA period (SCHEDULE_PERIOD_TRIM) so the walk drifts down to the arrival floor; SCHEDULE_MAX_LEAD_MS 150->60; LEAD_MS 30 removed (redundant with the render delay, which already sizes to 1.5 x p95 gap + a frame); RENDER_DELAY_MIN/MAX_MS named, values unchanged (20/120); TELEMETRY_HZ 25->50 (four 5 ms pacer ticks, under the motion channel's 60 Hz max_rate_hz; SPEC 6.7 refuses per wish only on channel/access/count, SPEC 10.2 clamps to max_rate_hz, so never a refused rate; 60 Hz truncates to 16 ms and the tick rounds it to 20, i.e. 50 Hz under a 60 Hz grant). Sim predicts ~55-70 ms client lag at 50 Hz. Unverified: whether the P4 delivers 50 Hz evenly under full subscription load (S3 measured 40/50 Hz worse than 25; the T18 reconstruction landed after that measurement). Owed: live lag_probe.py --dump + rAF sampler in Chromium AND in phosphor.exe (WebView2); if 50 Hz paces badly, fall back to 25 and keep the telebuf fix.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: code side landed in 5e7b206; measurement owed (live hub lag_probe.py --dump + rAF sampler of .hn-val.mono, Chromium and phosphor.exe/WebView2 separately).

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-03 with test/latency-probe.mjs (5b892bc), Chromium, 30 s per run, 'before' = 5e7b206 reverted in the same build. valencesim 0.1.6-p4hub (0.8 Hz +-20 mm sine through the motion door): client wire->paint 150.0 -> 101.1 ms, per-frame p50 149.3 -> 99.9, p95 185.6 -> 132.1; end to end 195.7 -> 144.9 (p95 231 -> 176); hub 45.7/43.8 ms; amplitude ratio 1.000, corr 0.997. P4 192.168.1.118 0.1.6-p4hub-bench: MultiFunPlayer holds the stream source (owner1 308856519) and was driving, so the probe's own sine was refused and those runs are void; measured with --watch instead (no token, no motion, MFP's motion as the signal; the method agrees with the sine fit within 1 ms on the sim's series): client 199.0 -> 102.0 ms, per-frame p50 203.3 -> 102.5, p95 227.9 -> 341.7 (the arbitrary signal makes the per-frame p95 a crossing-ambiguity ceiling, not lag). What is left (~100 ms) is the render delay (86-93 ms = 1.5 x arrival p95 gap + a frame), and that gap is the hub's: 0x1100 arrives every 46.8 ms on the sim and 35 ms on the P4 at a 50 or 60 Hz grant (filed Nucleus val-7ur). TELEMETRY_HZ 50 buys nothing until the hubs deliver at the grant. Stays open for: phosphor.exe (WebView2) via --cdp, which needs the shell relaunched with WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222 (operator's running shell was not touched), and the hub-term on the P4 when nothing else owns the stream.

description:

title: Rust shell: UDP discovery magic/port were re-pinned to the Valence registry
description:
src-tauri/src/discovery.rs is a HAND-TRANSCRIBED copy of registry udp_discovery. At carve-out it still held the pre-rename values (port 21328, magic 'SLOP'); the registry now pins port 22096 and magic 'VLNC' (0x56 0x4C 0x4E 0x43). Changed here to match the registry, which is the one home (C-1).

Consequence, operator-veto-able: this shell can no longer discover a hub still speaking the old magic/port, which is every build of the archived S3 firmware. Verify against ValenceDrive once its discovery side is re-pinned too.

The old repo checked this by tools/spec-drift.sh, which did not come across. Either port that check here or accept the hand copy as unguarded (T20 says an unguarded hand copy drifts silently).
notes: Inventoried every registry-derived constant hand-copied in Phosphor outside the imported Valence JS client: discovery.rs PORT/MAGIC (already re-pinned, matched), ble-ws.js BLE_SERVICE/CHAR_C2H_WRITE/CHAR_H2C_NOTIFY (still pre-rename SLOP/SYNC UUIDs, drifted), ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT (still 21328, drifted). No frame-type literals (0x1E/0x1F), ws_subprotocol, or mdns_service are hand-spelled anywhere in src/ or src-tauri/. Wrote test/check-registry-pins.mjs: parses registry.yaml's udp_discovery and ble_identity blocks with a small line-oriented scalar parser (no yaml dep) and greps the 2 Rust + 3 JS pins for a match, failing with file:line and both values. Rust cannot import JS so it stays gated by this script permanently (stated in the file banner); ws_subprotocol/mdns_service are already codegen-emitted and nothing in Phosphor spells them, so nothing to convert to an import. Fixed the 2 drifted files to match the registry (same C-1 precedent as this bead's own discovery.rs fix): ble-ws.js UUIDs 534c4f50-5359-4e43-... -> 56414c45-4e43-4531-..., ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT 21328 -> 22096. Wired into npm run check (also added check:pins). npm run check: all green (device-knowledge, registry-pins, settings-model). cargo check in src-tauri: Finished dev profile, zero errors/warnings.
close_reason: Staleness gate landed (test/check-registry-pins.mjs, wired into npm run check) and the two drifted hand-copies it found (ble-ws.js BLE UUIDs, ShellBar.svelte DISCOVERY_PORT) were fixed to match the registry. Rust pins have no import escape and stay gated by the script; check green, cargo check clean.

description: Every Playwright suite loads the single dist/index.html, which forced one worktree per lane. A --dist <dir> (or env) parameter on test/run-suites.mjs and the suites removes that constraint. Do after the layout pass lands (the lanes edit the suites).

title: Comet trail is not smooth
description: Operator 2026-10-05: the position comet (RailWidget drawComet, fed by telebuf's interpolated instant) does not move smoothly. RailWidget already measures marker displacement per frame (the 'marker smoothness is MEASURED per frame' harness near line 630): read that first. Suspects: the telemetry.position grant rate vs the telebuf interpolation window, the 850 ms trail resampling, and shadowBlur cost dropping frames on the integrated GPU. description:

EVIDENCE: Valence spec/RFC-QUEUE.md RFC-044 (lines ~2677-2719, status Draft, deprioritized); Nucleus motion-input and motion-segment STREAM channels (ValenceCatalog.h:819, :862).

ACCEPTANCE: blocked on RFC-044 acceptance (never code against an unaccepted clause). Once accepted: a kernel module that ingests TCode lines (shell: serial/WebSocket source) and emits segments through the session with the normal ownership and safety gates, never around them; decline when the hub advertises no stream channel.
notes: Orchestrator ruling 2026-09-25 (veto-able): the TCode adapter stays as an EXAMPLE PLUGIN (plugins/examples/tcode-adapter). It uses no RFC-044 wire clause (RFC-044 defines none) and only existing intent surfaces, so 'never code against an unaccepted clause' is not triggered; Prime Rule holds because it writes through the host intent path. Promotion beyond example status waits on RFC-044/RFC-061 acceptance and the STREAM publish path (ph-vdk.26, Valence rfc-ts3).
close_reason: Shipped as the example plugin plugins/examples/tcode-adapter (ddf6d04, 0a4e670): Rust loopback TCP line service, L0 parse, submitMotion onto the granted samples STREAM with setpoint fallback.
